name: v0.5.7-beta.2 — VoiceStudio
body:
### Installer signing

| Platform | Signing |
|---|---|
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | ✅ Signed with Developer ID and notarized by Apple |
| macOS (Intel) | ✅ Signed with Developer ID and notarized by Apple |
| Windows x64 | ⚠️ Unsigned: SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your PC"; choose More info → Run anyway |
| Windows ARM64 | ⚠️ Unsigned: SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your PC"; choose More info → Run anyway |
| Linux x64 | — Linux packages are not code-signed |

**Highlights**

- Preview iOS and Android apps that run VoiceStudio on your phone, offline after downloading the models
- Opt-in Beta update channel: get fixes early from Settings → Updates, and roll onto the next stable release automatically

### Changed

- The sidebar is a slim icon rail beside each section's own pane: Home and Clone get a Saved voices / Recent takes column, Design gets a Saved voices tab, and the full navigation is one click away (#3234)
- The GitHub button in the top bar is one Star pill with the live count, and the star fills gold on hover (#3234)
- Stories, Audiobook and Dubbing show their saved projects in a Projects tab beside the controls, so your files are one tap away wherever you work (#3234)
- Source ZIPs and tarballs omit scam-moderation attack examples; Git clones and CI retain their regression tests (#3237)
- Maintainers can upload public source ZIPs or individual files with `make virustotal`, or scan a branch through the manual VirusTotal Actions workflow (#3237)

- Small models now install with as little as 2 GB spare disk; the setup check only warns below 10 GB instead of blocking (#2969)
- iOS Home shows Electron's contributor avatars, Dub is redesigned around one source card with animated icons, and the iOS bottom dock is icon-only (#2969)
- Model licence review on iOS and Android opens with a plain summary, rights rows and licence links; the raw terms move under Exact terms (#2969)
- Phone apps now use the app ID `sh.voicestudio.mobile`; a preview build installed before installs alongside as a new app, so pair it again and remove the old one (#3194)

### Added

- The phone apps run speech, dictation, voice cloning and dubbing on the phone itself, offline once you download the models; pairing a computer is optional ([guide](docs/mobile.md)) (#2969)
- Beta update channel: choose Stable or Beta under Settings → Updates; betas are `-beta.N` prereleases that never reach Stable users, and Docker gets matching `:beta` tags ([guide](docs/update-channels.md)) (#3175)

- Preview iOS and Android companion apps: drive your own VoiceStudio from your phone (speak, voices and cloning, dubbing, dictation) after pairing by QR code; build from source for now ([guide](docs/mobile.md)) (#2965)
- Smart Fit speed limits: set the fastest and slowest speed dubbing may apply to a line, from the Timing section (#3026) — thanks @MoonDragon-MD!

### Fixed

- Saved dub loads confirm before replacing unsaved work, recheck edits made during loading and stop when you leave the workspace (#3234)
- Large VirusTotal uploads upgrade the documented legacy upload URL to HTTPS before sending files or credentials (#3238)

- iPhone: tapping Play right after generating speech starts playback instead of doing nothing (#3233)

- Android app icons preserve transparent waveform paths from the shared logo, including themed icons (#2969)
- Speak keeps your script when switching between the phone and computer on Android (#2969)
- Phone dubbing no longer speaks the wrong words when a quiet reference clip is not recognised (#2969)
- Refined iOS navigation, voice libraries, grouped creation forms and licence sheets with native controls, accessible text and explicit cancellation (#2969)
- Phone apps open on an Electron-style Home dashboard with shared artwork, workspace shortcuts, recent audio, saved voices and resumable dubbing projects (#2969)
- Phone video dubbing uses a supported AAC bitrate and preserves playable audio, rotation and synthetic-audio metadata (#2969)
- Phone dub playback restores sound after dictation on iOS and keeps the video visible when switching results on Android (#2969)
- Stereo reference files and dictation inputs keep both channels when converted to mono on iOS (#2969)
- Android dubbing errors remain visible when worker updates arrive while their receipt is being saved (#3031)

- iOS reserves storage across simultaneous model downloads and keeps saved speech paired with the submitted text (#2969)
- TestFlight builds prepare the on-device inference runtimes before archiving the iPhone app (#2969)

- Phone models can be reaccepted offline without downloading again, and Android dubbing preserves short audio gaps and overlaps (#2969)
- App icon, tray icons and in-app logo no longer show a black band behind the waveform (#3221)
- Speed/quality changes finish as soon as they are saved, even while the clone controls are still loading (#3031)
- Speed / quality in the sidebar is a simple slider again; models and hardware fit open in a popover on hover, click or change, so the simplest view leaves the sidebar bottom free (#3031)
- The Latest take panel is more compact: file details, render time and Check audio share one row (#3031)
- The sidebar's Saved voices and Recent takes buttons both keep their labels instead of collapsing the inactive one to an icon (#3031)
- On macOS full screen the sidebar logo moves into the freed corner, the compact rail drops its traffic-light gap (#3031)


- Bug reports no longer risk freezing the app while looking for your tools: the Node-version folder scan now runs off the main thread (#3180)
- Bug reports no longer freeze the app when the tool search or a drive stalls, and free disk is only borrowed from a parent folder when the install folder doesn't exist yet (#3179)
- Model licence dialog is wider and scrolls as one area with the buttons pinned, and follows macOS, Windows and Linux dialog conventions (#3160)
- Bug reports now include your OS, memory, free disk and whether the Python runtime exists, even when the backend never started, plus flags for risky install paths such as OneDrive or non-ASCII folders (#3156)
- Bug reports no longer hang on a stalled drive, and report free disk and the uv tool correctly on first run and in source checkouts (#3170)
- Older synthesized takes play again with accurate play/pause controls after a newer generation (#3102)
- Generation-complete notifications appear above the workspace instead of covering synthesis controls (#3102)
- Generated speech no longer starts and ends with silence, and `[pause]` markers give exactly the pause you asked for (Raw preset and explicit durations untouched) (#3080)
- Engine sidecars no longer load PyTorch just to answer the Test Engine ping, and a failed test logs its reason locally (#3026) — thanks @tekay-de!

### Fixed

- Windows runtime refresh no longer fails with `EPERM` on a locked backend folder (OneDrive, antivirus): it updates the files in place; the missing-Python-environment message now names the exact folder and tells non-checkout installs to use the installer (#3023) — thanks @afraniohugo, @javalovelinux-cmd and @eduardpp00!

### Fixed

- The install location chosen in first-run setup now also holds your data, model cache and temp files instead of quietly filling `C:`, and the setup screen shows each path (#2971, #3035)
- Supertonic-3's preset voices can be picked in the voice controls and are used for generation (#2938, #3035)

- `OMNIVOICE_ENGINES_DIR` moves engine venvs and the audio.cpp runtime to another drive; the default location is unchanged (#3024)

### Fixed

- The installed app now rebuilds a Python environment that antivirus or disk cleanup removed, once per launch with the usual setup progress, instead of stopping at a setup error; your voices and projects are untouched (#3032) — thanks @afraniohugo and @javalovelinux-cmd!

### Changed

- The sponsor footer is gone from the app; sponsored integrations keep a Featured badge on their card in Integrations (#3031)

### Docs

- `SPONSORS.md` now states what each sponsorship tier gives, when recognition starts, and what sponsorship does not buy, and the README and inquiry form point to it (#3172)
- OmniVoice GGUF docs state that the installers do not ship its native binary yet (#3026) — thanks @DestinyQJY!
- Contributor guides and the pull request template explain how to sign the CLA before opening a first pull request (#2676)

### Fixed

- macOS builds without a Developer ID are now signed ad hoc so the bundle signature is valid, and the shell installer clears quarantine, repairs an invalid signature of older releases, names an unreadable disk image, and tells Intel Mac users the backend needs Apple Silicon (#3033, #2763, #2829, #2681)
- A "Generation failed" log line now says where it was raised and which error caused it, and the out-of-memory advice mentions picking another GPU, so these reports can be told apart (#2895, #2684, #2666, #2626, #2622, #2580, #3034)

### CI

- Release notes list everyone who contributed since the last stable release automatically, instead of only the people thanked by hand (#3242)
- Release notes list each platform's installer signing as measured on the build, and a macOS build that would open as "damaged" can no longer be released, and macOS releases are signed with the Developer ID again (#3241, #3243)
- The owner can let named maintainers publish releases while Windows installers are still unsigned (#3236)
- Android release and Play builds share an increasing version code to prevent reused or decreasing build numbers (#2969)
- Phone build resources keep notice hashes and localized text intact on Windows (#2969)
- New `mobile-release` workflow builds signed Android and iOS apps and drafts a GitHub prerelease with the APK, AAB and IPAs (#2969)
- The `mobile` workflow builds the pinned on-device runtimes for both apps (#2969)
- The main test step runs in parallel with pytest-xdist, about 3 minutes faster per CI run (#3223)

- Interactive release helper: pick stable or beta, draft or publish, and confirm by typing the tag (`scripts/release.py`) (#3187)
- Release helper choices are arrow-key menus (#3190)
- Desktop UI tests no longer fail at random when Electron's debugger takes the dev proxy's port; the proxy now binds an OS-assigned port (#3126)
- Desktop request-guard self-tests stay deterministic when app requests arrive during cleanup (#2676)

- New `mobile` workflow builds and tests both phone apps; a contract test fails when their theme or API description drifts from the desktop app (#2965)

- iOS TestFlight workflow: maintainers can upload a signed iPhone build for internal testers from `main` ([guide](docs/mobile.md#testflight-maintainers)) (#3188)
- iOS TestFlight builds declare their exempt encryption, so uploads no longer wait on the export compliance question (#3230)
- iOS TestFlight uploads with on-device inference pass App Store validation, and the workflow checks every bundled framework before uploading (#3235)
- Beta and stable release builds no longer fail when a slow build machine runs the app's tests (#3232)
- Android Play internal testing workflow: the matching signed Android upload from `main`, and beta versions no longer break the Android build ([guide](docs/mobile.md#play-internal-testing-maintainers)) (#3189)

- Gallery preview fallback smoke no longer flakes when a slower runner reads the playing clip in several byte ranges (#3018)

### Contributors

Thanks to everyone who contributed to this release: @debpalash, @velixio, @rudycelekli, @swadhinbiswas, @kevin9327, @nvtoan0201-swe, @nirmalchatur, @BichengWang, @chiarorosa, @emreisik95, @abdullah-rashid62, @drakeo338, @FenjuFu, @Vaishnavi220506, @Nikhi00718, @shivsin25, @bercedev, @Cengokill, @DeryFerd, @ege-arhan, @eltociear, @HoneyTyagii, @li-lizhe, @mvanhorn, @NN708, @Raunaksplanet, @vincentfranstyo, @JoshuaWIls, @strauss-visuals, @Yi-111-a

name: v1.15.0 - Standalone install, update dry run
body:
## What's New in v1.15.0

You can now install OpenSpec without Node.js, using one command, and `openspec update` can now show what it would change before changing anything.

### New

- **Standalone install** - Install OpenSpec with one command and no Node.js: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/main/scripts/binary/install.sh | sh` on macOS and Linux, or `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/main/scripts/binary/install.ps1 | iex` on Windows. Every release now ships binaries for macOS, Linux (glibc and musl) and Windows on x64 and arm64, with `SHA256SUMS`. npm and the other package managers keep working as before.
- **`openspec update --dry-run`** - Reports the files an update would add, change or delete without writing anything; add `--json` for machine-readable output.

### Improved

- **Faster `--json` commands** - `status`, `instructions`, `new change`, `templates`, `validate` and `schema` no longer load the spinner package when run with `--json`, so they start a little faster. Output is unchanged.
- **`openspec feedback`** - Filed issues now match the bug form, and the manual-submission link opens the bug form with your message, version and environment filled in.

### Fixed

- **`openspec new change`** - The progress line now names the schema the change is actually created with, instead of always saying `spec-driven`.
- **`/opsx:verify`** - A REMOVED requirement is matched to its baseline by its exact name, so a similarly named replacement is no longer mistaken for it.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/compare/v1.14.3...v1.15.0

name: v3.23.2 — Integrity checks read only the cited version, Stage 2.5 always runs, and adapter, announce, and Windows repairs
body:
> **Repairs; no new skill. One prompt-level change has a small behaviour check, and the others are unmeasured:** v3.23.2 makes the Stage 2.5 and 4.5 claim checks compare a claim only with the version of a work that the manuscript cites (#1006). When that version cannot be read, the check records an access note and asks for its PDF instead of reading a working paper or preprint. In one synthetic fixture run six times (three sessions each on Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1, web tools off), every session followed the rule. A prior integrity report no longer lets a pipeline run skip Stage 2.5; the run attaches it as context (#995). A missing required input blocks the stage transition on every surface (#990), and the Socratic mentor's example no longer ranks the user's ideas (#992). The SessionStart announce shows the update reminder to the user, and the model-facing announce is about 2.1 KB shorter (#999). The Obsidian adapter accepts unquoted ISO dates and rejects boolean and superscript-digit years (#988, #989); six lints compare paths in POSIX form on Windows (#964, #978); the Pi wrapper composes with Pi's structured prompt sections (#985); and `CITATION.cff` gives the author's ORCID iD (#1007). Outside contributors wrote #978, #985, and #988.

### Changed

- **`CITATION.cff` gives the author's ORCID iD (#1007).** Zenodo reads the file when it archives a release, so later versions under the concept DOI link their creator to https://orcid.org/0009-0008-9523-0103. Versions already on Zenodo do not change.

### Fixed

- **The SessionStart announce shows the user what is meant for the user (#999).** `scripts/announce-ars-loaded.sh` sent everything through `additionalContext`, which reaches only the model, so the #544 update reminder never reached the user. Startup and clear now also set `systemMessage`: a one-line loaded notice, preceded by the update reminder when one is available. The model-facing startup announce replaces the 16-row command table, the agent table, and the token-budget line with one line of command names and one line of agent names (about 2.1 KB less per session); the command-invariants lint still checks every `/ars-*` token and the count. The skill-routing paragraph and the routing core are unchanged. Three tests in `scripts/test_ars_update_check.py` pin the new field.
- **Missing required inputs block the transition in the pipeline state machine too (#990).** The Missing Materials section of `academic-pipeline/references/pipeline_state_machine.md` let the user "skip (at own risk)" a required input, while `shared/handoff_schemas.md` Validation Rules (rule 5) and the state tracker's gap table block the transition. The section now follows the state tracker: a missing required input returns `HANDOFF_INCOMPLETE` and is backfilled before the next stage runs, a missing recommended input does not block and is reported, and integrity checks still cannot be skipped. The #528 content lock is updated.
- **The Socratic mentor's "direct answer" example no longer ranks the user's ideas (#992).** The example in `deep-research/agents/socratic_mentor_agent.md` said "your second idea actually has a lot of potential", which the Research-Question Authorship Boundary in the same file forbids. It now declines and asks which of the user's own directions they most want to understand, and why. The ideation-diversity non-production variant pins the new source hash. Prompt-level; the effect on model behaviour is unmeasured.
- **A prior integrity report no longer lets a pipeline run skip Stage 2.5 (#995).** `shared/handoff_schemas.md` Validation Rules (rule 11) and the `academic-pipeline/SKILL.md` Mid-Entry Protocol allowed a fresh, unmodified, user-confirmed report to skip Stage 2.5, while the orchestrator's Mid-Entry Material Passport Check required Stage 2.5 in every run and attached the prior report as context. All surfaces now follow the orchestrator: Stage 2.5 always runs before Stage 3, and a prior report that is `VERIFIED`, fresh, and on the current version is attached to the run as context. The same rule is stated in the orchestrator's mid-entry routing rules and the Stage 3 row of `academic-pipeline/references/mode_advisor.md`. `check_spec_consistency.py` pins the new rule-11 heading and body and the absence of the old skip wording in the four files; the #528 content locks are updated. Prompt-level; the effect on model behaviour is unmeasured.
- **Phase E checks a claim only against the version of a work that the manuscript cites (#1006).** Stage 2.5 and 4.5 source tracing (`academic-pipeline/references/claim_verification_protocol.md` E2, mirrored in `integrity_verification_agent.md`) could read a working paper or preprint when the cited version was not readable, and judge the claim against it, which produced both false flags and false passes. The check now identifies the cited version from the reference entry (and from `version_records.yaml` when present), never substitutes another version, and records `UNVERIFIABLE_ACCESS` with a request for the cited version's PDF when that version cannot be read, including an open-access page the agent cannot read. A reference entry that does not identify exactly one version gets the same note with `VERSION_INCONSISTENT_CITATION`, and an author-accepted manuscript stands in only when the reference cites it. For a claim with several sources, an access note on one source no longer hides a distortion found in another. Each evidence row names the version in its existing `source.display_label`, which the rendered table already prints; the evidence-row schema does not change. The orchestrator's checkpoint line asks for the cited version's PDF (content lock updated). `check_evidence_row_integration.py` pins the rules, and `scripts/test_phase_e_cited_version.py` pins that the row carrier records and renders the access outcome. Whether runs follow the rule is prompt-level. In one synthetic fixture run six times (three sessions each on Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1, web tools off), every session recorded the access note, asked for the cited version, and issued no verdict from the working paper that was readable.
- **The Obsidian adapter rejects a boolean year and a year written in superscript digits (#989).** `_coerce_year` in `scripts/adapters/obsidian.py` accepted `year: true` as an integer, because `bool` is a subclass of `int`, and wrote `year: true` to the corpus. A year string such as `'²⁰²⁴'` passed `str.isdigit()` and then raised `ValueError` in `int()`, which stopped the run before the passport was written. Both notes are now rejected with `year_unparseable` and the run continues. The string check uses `str.isdecimal()`, so years in other decimal scripts that `int()` reads are still accepted. A parametrized test in `scripts/adapters/tests/test_obsidian.py` covers both cases.
- **The Obsidian adapter accepts a year written as an unquoted ISO date (#987, #988, contributed by @harshajv7981).** `yaml.safe_load` turns `year: 2024-01-15` into a `datetime.date` before `_coerce_year` sees it, so the adapter rejected the note as `year_unparseable`, although its docstring lists that form as accepted; Obsidian's Properties panel writes Date properties this way. `_coerce_year` now takes the year from a date or datetime value. A regression test in `scripts/adapters/tests/test_obsidian.py` covers it.
- **The Pi wrapper composes ARS with Pi's structured prompt sections (#966, #985, contributed by @daniyyell-dev).** When the wrapper returned a rendered `systemPrompt`, Pi treated it as a complete override and could drop sections from other extensions, such as MCP instructions. When `event.systemPromptOptions` is available, the wrapper now filters package-owned skills while ARS is inactive and adds an `ars_compatibility` section while it is active; stopping ARS removes only that section. Hosts without the structured API keep the string and array fallback from #880. Unit tests and an opt-in integration test against Pi 1.1.0 and 1.3.0 cover it.
- **Windows: six lints compare repository paths in POSIX form (#964, #978, contributed by @daniyyell-dev).** `check_684_review_criteria_binding.py`, `check_collaboration_depth_rubric.py`, `check_content_coverage_advisory_integration.py`, `check_cross_document_consistency_advisory_integration.py`, `check_decision_contract.py`, and `check_tortured_phrase_screening_integration.py` compared `str(Path)`, which uses `\` on Windows, with forward-slash paths, and failed on a correct tree. They now use `Path.as_posix()`. The new tests pass Windows-style paths into each lint's comparison, so the Ubuntu CI fails if a conversion is reverted.

name: Reasonix Studio v2.50.0
body:
本版让子代理可以在工作台里开成标签页读完整记录，设置里新增导航入口管理、计费方式和放大设置窗口，正文栏可拖宽，并修复多处卡住、显示与对齐问题。

## 新增

- 正文栏左右边线可以拖动，两侧同时等量变宽或收窄；缩到“适宜阅读”为止，放到窗口全宽为止，被挡住的侧栏按各自设定的比例让位。关联 #14198 by @imcreazy。
- 反馈表单的正文可以切到「预览」，先看 Markdown 渲染的样子；公开的议题仍把原文放在代码块里。修复 #14248 fixed in #14255。
- 设置 → 外观 →「导航入口」可隐藏或调整图标栏和侧栏里的入口，两处同步；会话、反馈、账号和设置始终保留。关联 #14236、#14190。
- 设置窗口头部多了「放大设置窗口」按钮，可铺满整个窗口、内容区同步变宽；选择会记住，下次打开保持。修复 #14272 fixed in #14271。
- 桌面端可连自己部署的远程网关（REASONIX_REMOTE_URL、REASONIX_REMOTE_GATEWAY_ID），手机网页按授权里的网关地址连接；非 wss:// 地址会被拒绝。关联 #14282。
- 从“子代理”面板打开子代理，会在工作台开成标签页，读内核记录的完整对话（运行中持续刷新），工具步骤可折叠、可同时开多个；找不到记录时仍用原对话框。关联 #13523 fixed in #14291。
- 连接编辑页可选“计费方式”（按量计费或订阅套餐），订阅套餐的用量会按所填价格折算成估算值单独显示，不计入实际花费。关联 #13276。
- 设置 → 工具与权限第二项提供「AI 文件交付卡片」开关，支持搜索并保存用户选择，重新打开会话生效。关联 #14063 by @SivanCola。

## 变更

- 侧栏会记住你折叠过的项目，重新打开界面后仍保持折叠；新项目默认展开，不替你做决定。关联 #14195 by @lancy69。
- 设置打开时，背后的内容被更深的平面遮罩压下去，设置面板更突出；没有使用实时模糊。关联 #14196 by @lancy69。
- 正文两侧的拖拽边线常驻一条短细线，看得出这里可以拖；长对话里回到顶部与跳到最新的提示不再一移就消失；两个把手也能用键盘调宽。关联 #14198 by @imcreazy。
- 隐藏图标栏时，侧栏列出与图标栏相同的入口（文件、工具与权限、扩展、记忆、远程），名称统一；两处读同一份清单。关联 #14236。
- 并行写入的“乐观模式”现在默认开启：没声明写入范围的子代理和写入不再占住整个工作区；已选过“严格”的不受影响，可在设置里关闭。关联 #14240。
- 你对某个对话选的“本会话允许”现在随这个对话保存，恢复或重新打开这个对话后不再重复询问；仍只对该对话有效，可随时撤销。关联 #14243。

<!-- lang:en -->

This release opens sub-agents as Workbench tabs with their full record, adds navigation-entry management, a billing choice and an enlarged Settings window, lets you drag the reading column wider, and fixes a number of stalls, display and alignment problems.

## New

- The reading column's edges can be dragged: both sides widen or narrow by the same amount, between the readable measure and the window. Refs #14198 by @imcreazy.
- the feedback form's body can switch to a Markdown preview; a public issue still shows the original text in a code block. Fixes #14248 fixed in #14255.
- Settings → Appearance → Navigation entries hides or reorders the shortcuts in the icon rail and sidebar together; sessions, feedback, account and settings stay. Refs #14236, #14190.
- the settings window has an Enlarge button that fills the whole window and widens its content; the choice is remembered. Fixes #14272 fixed in #14271.
- the desktop host can use a remote gateway you run (REASONIX_REMOTE_URL, REASONIX_REMOTE_GATEWAY_ID); the phone page follows the grant's gateway; non-wss:// relays are refused. Refs #14282.
- a sub-agent opened from the Sub-agents panel is now a Workbench tab reading the kernel's full record (live while it runs), foldable, several at once; no record keeps the dialog. Refs #13523 fixed in #14291.
- the connection editor now has a Billing choice (pay as you go or subscription plan); a plan's usage is shown as a separate estimate at the entered prices, never as money spent. Refs #13276.
- a searchable AI file delivery switch is the second item in Tools & permissions. It saves your choice for reopened sessions. Refs #14063 by @SivanCola.

## Changed

- the sidebar remembers which projects you folded and keeps them folded when the interface reopens; new projects still start expanded. Refs #14195 by @lancy69.
- while Settings is open, the content behind it is pushed back by a stronger flat scrim, so Settings stands out; no live blur is used. Refs #14196 by @lancy69.
- The reading column's edges carry a standing mark, the two pills keep their tip while the pointer moves, and the handles answer the arrow keys. Refs #14198 by @imcreazy.
- with the icon rail hidden, the sidebar now lists the same destinations as the rail (Files, Tools and permissions, Extensions, Memory, Remote) under the same names, from one list. Refs #14236.
- optimistic mode for parallel writes is on by default, so writers with no declared scope no longer hold the whole workspace; a saved strict choice is kept. Refs #14240.
- "Allow for this session" is now saved with its conversation, so resuming or reopening it no longer asks again; it still covers only that conversation and can be revoked. Refs #14243.
- AI file delivery defaults on; explicit off choices remain off. Newly opened sessions add its tool schema and may incur one cold prefix. Refs #14063 by @SivanCola.

## Fixed

- the work-mode menu now labels the unavailable mode “Ask (Not implemented)” so it does not imply a missing configuration step. Mode switching and Ask's disabled state are unchanged. Refs #14028 fixed in #14093 by @lancy69.
- with the conversation column narrow (workbench open), the buttons under the composer stay on one row: the mode button collapses sooner and the model name shrinks. Refs #14156.
- a session billed in more than one currency no longer shows one summed figure under a single symbol; the meter and cost panel show one amount per currency. Refs #14178 by @chuiwenwei.
- a one-shot scheduled run that missed its time no longer stays Active; it shows as expired, so Renew no longer reports success when nothing will run. Refs #14179 by @chuiwenwei.
- in the terminal, r and /queue retry no longer re-send a recovered queue entry that may already have run; they say why and suggest checking the transcript or deleting it. Refs #14180 by @chuiwenwei.
- importing legacy sessions no longer moves or deletes a session that another window has open; it is left in place and settled on a later import. Refs #14181 by @chuiwenwei.
- the meter under the composer labelled the whole session's spend as "This turn"; it now shows "This session" and the last turn's own amount. Refs #14200.
- the queue itself now refuses to retry a recovered entry that may already have run, including retries made through the API or ACP, so an instruction is not run twice. Refs #14202.
- a long command in the delivery receipt card no longer fills the card; it shows its first line with an ellipsis, and the whole command is in the hover text. Refs #14204.
- with the icon rail hidden, sidebar rows line up icons and labels on one vertical line and share one 12px regular label style; New session and Send feedback are no longer bold. Refs #14207.
- the settings tool list now describes the remaining built-in tools (search, file edits, sub-agents, memory, peers) in the interface language, not model-facing English. Refs #14208.
- pasting a screenshot into the feedback form no longer does nothing after clicking a blank part of it, and an image the clipboard offers as an item is taken too. Refs #14210.
- the settings sheet is taller so its whole menu shows on a 1080p screen, the Memory icon lines up with its label, and the run analysis view keeps one name instead of "trajectory". Refs #14211.
- the scheduled runs page can trust the open project itself, so a project that never showed the trust prompt, or was declined earlier, no longer leaves you stuck. Refs #14216.
- the sidebar rows now share one label colour, and New session no longer has a filled background at rest. Refs #14221.
- the top bar's Run analysis icon is now a pulse line the same size and weight as its neighbours, instead of a small half-circle gauge. Fixes #14222 fixed in #14269.
- with the rail hidden, sidebar icons match the project folders and the logo the labels; session tabs centre their text; top rows lose hints; the avatar is one rounded square. Refs #14226.
- the "show in file manager" button now uses an open-folder icon instead of an arrow that read as share or external link. Refs #14227.
- the workbench bar puts the wide toggle at its left edge and the full-size toggle at its right edge instead of between the tabs. Refs #14229.
- the model is now told a sub-agent is not a new session: it dispatches it, the answer returns here, and nesting is bounded by `max_subagent_depth`. Refs #14247.
- a refused read now says which path was refused and whether it is outside the folders the session may read or on your forbidden-read list, not just "permission denied". Refs #14252.
- My feedback shows its last list at once and refreshes behind it; level, account and the leaderboard sit behind one collapsed row loaded on open instead of filling the first screen. Refs #14254.
- a skill step in the execution process now shows which skill it ran instead of just `run_skill`. Fixes #14256 fixed in #14259.
- after the kernel refuses a request the shell now checks this launch's credential cookie and restores it if missing, so no relaunch is needed. Refs #14260.
- when a plugin's runtime command is not an executable program (such as a `.sh` script on Windows), the error now says the plugin must ship a native executable. Refs #14263.
- choosing a reasoning depth that sends the same request as the current one (such as High when Auto resolves to High) now shows at once, not after a restart. Fixes #14173 fixed in #14265.
- on the paid search, network egress and MCP sign-in approval cards, the note under "Always allow" now says where the answer is actually kept instead of calling it a permission rule. Refs #14242.
- the settings text for sessions writing one project and for sub-agent write scope now matches the new default (optimistic mode) instead of saying "strict by default". Refs #14240.
- the sub-agent tool's description the model reads now describes writes with no declared scope under the new default (optimistic mode), not as claiming the whole workspace. Refs #14240.
- sidebar labels sat higher than their icons, and the Tools/Extensions/Memory/Remote icons were bolder and larger than the others; both are now level and matched. Refs #14266.
- with a command typed in full (/reload) beside longer ones sharing its name (/reload-cmd), Enter completed the longer one; the typed one is now listed first and Enter sends it. Fixes #14302 fixed in #14304.

## Upgrade notes

- Optimistic parallel writes are on by default, so sub-agents that declare no write paths no longer hold the whole workspace; turn it off in Settings to keep the strict behaviour. Refs #14240.
- The AI file-delivery tool is on by default, so the first session after upgrading has one cache miss; turn it off under Settings, Tools and permissions. Refs #14063 by @SivanCola.

body:
<!--
STYLE: follows the v1.3.1 release body (title, version/date line, framing intro, Highlights ->
Upgrading Notes -> Fixed -> Security -> Validation -> Installing -> Contributors -> Full Changelog;
bolded operative sentence then dense prose; refs inline as #NNNN; operator-facing; no emoji),
scaled down for a fix-only patch release: no Added or Changed section, because nothing was added.

SPAN: v1.3.1 -> v1.3.2 = the CHANGELOG sections [1.3.2], [1.3.2-rc.3], [1.3.2-rc.2] and
[1.3.2-rc.1] at the v1.3.2 tag (9b65b9e19), cross-checked against `git log v1.3.1..v1.3.2` and
the PRs it references. The v1.3.2 tree is the v1.3.2-rc.3 tree plus the version stamp and release
metadata. The proxied backup family, `bd purge --wisps-plane`/`--limit`, the #6716 fan-in recheck,
`bd sql` parser classification, proxied `bd show --watch`, `bd types`, the clean-exit proxy
retirement and authoritative `BEADS_DIR` all shipped in v1.3.1; they appear here only where
v1.3.2 fixes them (purge live-dependent chain, auto-backup watermark, recheck publication,
purge --limit hint). The doc re-review markers (#7267, #7268) are docs-only and not listed.

Every claim traces to that CHANGELOG or to a merged PR. Validation cites only runs that were looked
up: the tag's Release / Migration Test Harness / Cross-Version Smoke runs, the PR and Nightly runs
on the hotfix/1.3.1 PRs, and the Gas City v1.5.1 RC Gate. The goreleaser "## Changelog" commit
list is dropped, as v1.3.0 and v1.3.1 did.
-->

# Beads v1.3.2

**v1.3.2** — the second patch release on the 1.3 line. Released 2026-10-24, cut from
`hotfix/1.3.1` at `9b65b9e19`. It ships exactly the code that was qualified as `v1.3.2-rc.3`; the
only change since that candidate is the version stamp.

There is **no schema migration**, and the embedded Dolt engine is unchanged (Dolt 2.2.0). Upgrading
from v1.3.1 or any v1.3.2 release candidate is a binary swap. If you are coming from v1.3.0 or
earlier, read the [v1.3.1 release notes](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/releases/tag/v1.3.1)
first — everything in them applies, and this release adds to it.

This is a fix-only release. It closes two ways v1.3.1's new retention and backup paths could lose
data, makes the post-commit blocked-state recheck safe under concurrent writes, lets a
least-privilege Dolt user write again, removes an export stall on large wisp sets, and rebuilds with
Go 1.26.10 and patched dependencies. It also carries an upgrade note for every store that crossed
migration 0059 under bd 1.3.0 or later: read it before you upgrade.

## Highlights

- **`bd purge` no longer deletes the closed root of a chain that still has live work under it**
  (#7041, fixes #7031). v1.3.1's live-dependent protection only covered a closed bead a live bead
  pointed at directly, so an orchestrator's `bd purge --wisps-plane --older-than ...` retention
  sweep could delete a closed root above a closed child above an open grandchild, orphaning both.
  Protection now propagates up the whole closed chain.
- **Auto-backup never claims a commit the snapshot does not contain** (#7044, fixes #7032). The
  watermark is read before the sync, so a commit that lands mid-sync stays pending for the next
  backup instead of being skipped as "no changes".
- **The fan-in recheck no longer reverts concurrent writes** (#7146, backport of #6876, fixes
  #7030). On the Dolt server backend, the post-commit blocked-state recheck could write rows other
  sessions had just committed back to their earlier values. It now runs in its own transaction and
  publishes its Dolt commit after that transaction commits.
- **A least-privilege Dolt user can write again** (#7786, backport of #7322). `bd create --graph`,
  `bd mol wisp`, `bd history` and `bd recompute-blocked` no longer fail with `command denied` for a
  server user granted EXECUTE on only `dolt_add`/`dolt_commit`.
- **`bd export --all` no longer stalls on workspaces with many wisps** (#7603, backport of #6444,
  with #7785). Bulk readers read at most 200 ids per statement, and a repeated id is read once.
- **Security rebuild.** Release binaries build with Go 1.26.10 (#7732), and `x/net`, `x/crypto`,
  `grpc` and `thrift` are raised past every fixable advisory that reaches the binary (#6355,
  #7495).

## Upgrading Notes

- **After upgrading from bd 1.3.0 or earlier, run `bd recompute-blocked` once per workspace**
  (#7037). Migration 0059, first shipped in v1.3.0, recomputes the stored `is_blocked` flag with a
  recursive query. On Dolt servers older than 2.4.0, and on the embedded engine, a query-planner bug
  ([dolthub/dolt#11886](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/11886), fixed in Dolt 2.4.0) drops
  the query's `parent-child` edge filter, so blockedness spreads across every dependency type,
  including `relates-to`, `discovered-from` and `tracks`. Beads that are not blocked are marked
  blocked and silently disappear from `bd ready` and `bd list --ready`. The flag is stored, so the
  damage persists until it is recomputed, and **nothing in v1.3.2 repairs it automatically**. This
  applies to every workspace whose store crossed migration 0059 under bd 1.3.0 or later, which
  includes a workspace now on v1.3.1 that was first created by 1.2.x or earlier. The command is
  idempotent, reports `rows_corrected`, and changes nothing on a workspace that was not affected.
- **`bd purge` keeps more closed beads** (#7041). Every closed bead in a chain above a live bead is
  now kept and counted in `live_dependent_skipped`, on every backend. A retention sweep that used to
  delete such a root no longer does, so its purged count can drop.
- **The `bd purge --limit N` confirmation suggests a `--force` command that keeps `--limit`**
  (#7540, fixes #7534). The suggested command used to drop `--limit`, so running it as printed
  deleted every eligible row instead of N. If you copied that suggestion into a script, check it.
- **A negative `--older-than` that overflows is refused** on `bd purge` and `bd prune` (#7540, fixes
  #7524). A large negative day count, such as `--older-than=-213503d`, used to wrap to a small
  positive age and purge.
- **`bd export` fails when it cannot classify wisp-plane rows** (#7603). When the `wisps` table
  exists but its membership cannot be read, export now fails with `failed to classify wisp-plane
  rows` instead of silently exporting without wisp markers. Only a missing `wisps` table is
  tolerated.

## Fixed

- **`bd purge` keeps the whole closed chain above a live bead** (#7041, fixes #7031). Take a closed
  root R, a closed child S1 and an open grandchild S2. v1.3.1 protected S1, because S2 is live, but
  not R, because its only dependent S1 is closed, so purge deleted R and orphaned S1 and S2;
  `--dry-run` reported the same deletion. Protection now propagates through closed candidates until
  nothing changes, on the Dolt server, embedded and proxied backends.
- **The auto-backup watermark no longer runs ahead of the snapshot** (#7044, fixes #7032).
  Auto-backup read Dolt HEAD after the sync and recorded it as the newest commit backed up, so a
  commit that landed during the sync was recorded as backed up although the snapshot lacked it, and
  auto-backup then reported "no changes since last backup" until HEAD moved again. Only opted-in
  auto-backup (`backup.enabled: true`) was affected; `bd backup sync` records no commit watermark.
- **The post-commit blocked-state recheck no longer reverts concurrent writes** (#7146, backport of
  #6876, fixes #7030). v1.3.1's #6716 fan-in fix minted its Dolt commit while its own SQL
  transaction was still open. `DOLT_ADD` stages the table from the session's BEGIN-time root, so the
  commit could write `issues` rows that other sessions had just committed back to their BEGIN-time
  values. The recheck runs only when unblocking writes (closes, dependency removals, deletes) race,
  which is exactly when this matters. The recompute now runs alone in its own retried transaction
  and the Dolt commit is published after it. A failed trailing commit is counted as
  `post_tx_commit_dropped` and logged, instead of being reported as a recheck failure, because the
  flag repair itself is already committed.
- **A least-privilege Dolt user can write again** (#7786, backport of #7322). Two fresh-connection
  paths ran `CALL DOLT_CHECKOUT` even when the session was already on the requested branch: the
  fallback for the ignored-tables transaction, and the pinned connection used by long-timeout
  versioned reads and the blocked recompute. A server user granted EXECUTE on only
  `dolt_add`/`dolt_commit` is denied even that no-op checkout. The checkout now runs only when the
  session is on a different branch.
- **`bd export --all` no longer stalls on workspaces with many wisps** (#7603, backport of #6444).
  The bulk label, comment, dependency and issue readers sent every id in one `IN (...)` list, and
  Dolt's cost grows faster than linearly in the list length; one reported workspace stopped
  completing exports past about 21k wisps. The readers now read at most 200 ids per statement, and
  export reads the wisp-plane relations only for ids that are wisps. A repeated id is read once, so
  batching never duplicates or drops a row (#7785).
- **`bd purge --limit N` confirmation and `--older-than` overflow** (#7784, backport of #7540, fixes
  #7534 and #7524). See Upgrading Notes.

## Security

- **Release binaries build with Go 1.26.10** (#7787, backport of #7732), which distrusts the
  compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs in `crypto/x509`. `release.yml` uses uv 0.13.4, which ships
  the same distrust.
- **Dependency floors raised** (#7787): `golang.org/x/net` v0.60.0 and `golang.org/x/crypto`
  v0.57.0 (backport of #6355), and `google.golang.org/grpc` v1.83.2 and `github.com/apache/thrift`
  v0.24.0 (backport of #7495). `govulncheck` reported 16 reachable advisories on rc.2's module set
  and none on rc.3's, which is the v1.3.2 module set.

## Validation

- **v1.3.2 is the qualified rc.3 code.** The tag (`9b65b9e19`) differs from `v1.3.2-rc.3`
  (`0dee73e43`) only in the version stamp, the CHANGELOG, the `bd info` digest, and package and
  plugin version metadata.
- **Every fix landed on `hotfix/1.3.1` as a `cherry-pick -x` PR of a commit already on `main`,
  tested at its head.** The backport PRs (#7220, #7146, #7786, #7784, #7603, #7787) and the three
  RC prep PRs (#7221, #7461, #7788) each passed the full PR matrix of 120–122 checks, including the
  required `CI Gate / Required` gate that PRs into `hotfix/**` now run (#7198, ported in #7217). The
  promotion PR (#7809) passed 121 checks plus the Nightly Full Tests workflow by dispatch, once for
  the full test suite
  ([40042534271](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/actions/runs/40042534271)) and once for the
  PR Linux command suite
  ([40042536408](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/actions/runs/40042536408)).
- **The release pipeline completed green** (run
  [40044707863](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/actions/runs/40044707863)):
  `verify-version-consistency`, both goreleaser legs (linux and macOS), both package gates (MCP and
  npm), `publish-pypi`, `publish-npm` and release attestation. The tag-triggered Migration Test
  Harness ([40044708076](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/actions/runs/40044708076)) and
  Cross-Version Smoke Tests
  ([40044707912](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/actions/runs/40044707912)) also passed. 11
  assets were published: linux amd64/arm64, darwin amd64/arm64, windows amd64/arm64, freebsd amd64,
  android arm64, the contract corpus, an SPDX SBOM and checksums. All three release candidates also
  completed their release pipelines.
- **Qualified against a real downstream consumer before the tag.** Gas City's `hotfix/1.5.1`
  branch, pinned to `v1.3.2-rc.3`, passed its full RC Gate on the first attempt:
  [40034407401](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/actions/runs/40034407401), at
  `9d970f7cc8`. No job failed: the Linux CI parity tiers (including the beads topology
  acceptance, the bd CLI contract jobs against the current and minimum-supported bd, and a contract
  radar against beads `main`), acceptance A, B and C, all integration shards, tutorial goldens 1–6,
  the four worker-core providers, the goreleaser snapshot, and the full macOS regression set.

## Installing

Pre-compiled binaries for Linux, macOS (Intel & Apple Silicon), Windows (AMD64 & ARM64),
Android/Termux (ARM64), and FreeBSD are attached to this release.

**Homebrew (macOS/Linux):**
```bash
brew install beads
```

**Quick Install (macOS/Linux/FreeBSD):**
```bash
curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gastownhall/beads/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows (PowerShell):**
```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gastownhall/beads/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

**Manual Install:**
Download the appropriate binary for your platform below, extract it, and place it in your PATH.

Whichever method you use, run `which -a bd` afterwards. A second, older `bd` earlier in `PATH` is
the mixed-version fleet problem described in the v1.3.0 upgrading notes. Then run
`bd recompute-blocked` once per workspace if the first upgrading note applies to you.

## Contributors

Thanks to everyone who contributed to v1.3.2 (between `v1.3.1` and `v1.3.2`):

@bee-ghosttrack, @bourgois, @brandonmartin, @julianknutsen, @rjgeng

<!-- Commit authors in `git log v1.3.1..v1.3.2` (Bee = bee-ghosttrack, Karel Bourgois = bourgois,
Julian Knutsen = julianknutsen, Rongjun GENG = rjgeng), plus the author of backport PR #7603
(brandonmartin), mapped through the PR author via `gh api`. The gascityinc-randy[bot] author of
#7495's dependency bump and the "Gas City Adopt-PR" placeholder identity are excluded. -->

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/compare/v1.3.1...v1.3.2

name: v0.21.35
body:
# oh-my-codex v0.21.35

`0.21.35` is a patch release that fixes legacy recovery journal ownership and platform-aware replay logic.

This release addresses issues introduced in v0.21.34's shutdown preservation (#3896) where legacy recovery journals from other workers could block a healthy worker's shutdown. The fix scopes journal recovery to the owning worktree and enforces platform-aware naming conventions, preventing parent traversal attempts and ensuring module-only replay.

## Highlights

- **RESILIENCE: Worktree-scoped journal recovery (#3903):** A pending legacy (array-format) recovery journal owned by another worker no longer blocks a healthy worker's shutdown with `shutdown_worktree_preservation_failed`. This fixes a regression introduced by v0.21.34's shutdown preservation (#3896).
- **SAFETY: Platform-aware legacy journal ownership (#3904):** Legacy journal names beginning with `".."` are no longer treated as parent traversal attempts. Platform-aware ownership checking prevents cross-worker journal contamination.
- **MODULE ISOLATION: Modules-only replay (#3904):** Legacy journal replay is now enforced to operate only on modules, preventing accidental state corruption from misconfigured legacy journals.

## Compatibility

- No breaking API changes; recovery robustness improvements only.
- **Team runtime users:** If you experienced recovery journal blocking on shutdown in v0.21.34, this release resolves the issue.
- Existing sessions with pending legacy recovery journals will be handled correctly by the platform-aware logic.
- The fix improves legacy recovery robustness without changing the recovery API contract.

## Known issues

- #3898 (live-pin fix) is in progress (#3900); `Codex 0.164.0` hook validation was invalidated by `.omx-live-pin` files in the plugin cache. Workaround: manually clear `.omx-live-pin` from the cache if running Codex 0.164.0.

## Validation

- Pinned candidate `c6a41e75a04a77c7507b5987246abad80029ac9a` passed CI run at 02:17Z on 2026-10-24: 17 checks succeeded, 8 conditional checks skipped, no failures.
- Both macOS Ralplan preflight security jobs PASSED (not cancelled or failed).
- All local gates pass: build, typecheck, lint, and team runtime legacy recovery tests.
- All code review findings addressed.
- Ready for merge and release.

## Merged PR inventory

|---|---|---|
| [#3903](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-codex/pull/3903) | @shenyankm | fix(team): scope legacy recovery journals to the owning worktree |
| [#3904](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-codex/pull/3904) | @Claude Code | fix(team): platform-aware legacy journal ownership and modules-only replay |

## Contributors

Thanks to [@clawdbot](https://github.com/clawdbot) and [@Yeachan-Heo](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo) for contributing to this release.

**Full Changelog**: [`v0.21.34...v0.21.35`](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-codex/compare/v0.21.34...v0.21.35)

—

name: v0.21.34
body:
# oh-my-codex v0.21.34

`0.21.34` is a patch release that preserves worker worktrees when shutdown cannot save work (PR #3896).

This release fixes an issue where worker worktrees could be deleted during shutdown even when checkpointing or merging failed, or when the working directory contained ignored files. The shutdown process no longer deletes worker worktrees in these failure cases, allowing recovery state to be preserved for retries. Submodules, report provenance, and partial pane/prompt teardown are still handled correctly.

## Highlights

- **PRESERVATION: Worker worktrees survive shutdown failure (#3896):** When shutdown could not save work (checkpointing failure, merge failure, or ignored files present), the process would still delete worker worktrees, losing recovery state. The fix preserves worktrees in these cases, allowing retries with full state intact. This also resolves issue #3897.
- **Recovery state retention:** Shutdown failures no longer erase the work that was being preserved; recovery can be attempted on the next run.
- **Selective teardown (#3896):** Submodules, report provenance, and partial pane/prompt cleanup proceed independently; a failure in one component no longer cascades to worktree deletion.

## Compatibility

- No breaking API changes; shutdown resilience improvement only.
- **Team runtime users:** If shutdown failed to save work in earlier versions, worker worktrees were lost. Upgrade to v0.21.34 to preserve recovery state in shutdown failure cases.
- Existing sessions remain unaffected unless they experienced shutdown failures with ignored files or checkpointing errors.
- The fix improves robustness without changing the shutdown API contract.

## Known issues

- #3898 (live-pin fix) is in progress (#3900); `Codex 0.164.0` hook validation was invalidated by `.omx-live-pin` files in the plugin cache. Workaround: manually clear `.omx-live-pin` from the cache if running Codex 0.164.0.

## Validation

- Pinned candidate `bc7efc1c1c504b84a28cd4b24c1f3d6af08e6217` passed CI run at 20:16Z on 2026-10-24: 17 checks succeeded, 8 conditional checks skipped, no failures.
- Both macOS Ralplan preflight security jobs PASSED (not cancelled or failed).
- All local gates pass: build, typecheck, lint, and team runtime shutdown preservation tests.
- All code review findings addressed.
- Ready for merge and release.

## Merged PR inventory

| PR | Author | Title |
|---|---|---|
| [#3896](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-codex/pull/3896) | @shenyankm | fix(team): preserve worker worktrees when shutdown cannot save work |

## Contributors

Thanks to [@clawdbot](https://github.com/clawdbot), [@shenyankm](https://github.com/shenyankm), and [@Yeachan-Heo](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo) for contributing to this release.

**Full Changelog**: [`v0.21.33...v0.21.34`](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-codex/compare/v0.21.33...v0.21.34)

## 2026.10.7

### Highlights

- **Replay-safe session recovery:** interrupted sessions now retain recovery provenance and unfinished tool outcomes, stopped conversations retire terminal recovery residue before accepting the next message, rejected Claude CLI drafts stay out of final replies, large child-completion batches stay within requester context, and Codex previews no longer block replies after a context refresh. (#153728, #168764, #172068, #177716, #176682, #176783, #176675, #159715, #181801) Thanks @zhangguiping-xydt, @ruel225, @Oliver4Spot, @jjjhenriksen, @enki, @PennyVibe, @mbelinky, @RomneyDa, and @krjcolby-svg.
- **Safer update activation and recovery:** verified activations remain successful through later maintenance or ledger errors, interrupted package updates resume safely, post-activation Doctor waits are bounded, stale receipts cannot veto a valid repair, and Windows deep or 8.3 state paths no longer abort onboarding or migration. (#181166, #181307, #173862, #167459, #172768, #172769, #181389) Thanks @najef1979-code, @agroman1993, @shanselman, @RomneyDa, @dor-sr, @wangmiao0668000666, and @brucemccurdy.
- **Database and worker continuity:** maintenance refusals preserve peer readers and borrowers, incompatible retained agent databases stay isolated, empty transcript deletions skip unnecessary archive materialization, Bun admission deadlines remain thread-local, and worker shutdown completes after inventory retirement. (#175987, #179320, #170122, #171372, #172756, #168862) Thanks @LifeViwer, @Captain69G, @RomneyDa, @shanselman, @dor-sr, @wangmiao0668000666, and @brucemccurdy.
- **Backup and state durability:** snapshots retain supported legacy exec-approval policies, interrupted R2 verification and restores resume safely, config observation keeps the last-known-good snapshot during truncated writes, failed multi-file patches preserve earlier files, and Memory Wiki re-imports preserve human-authored notes. (#164297, #171292, #152565, #160409, #175707) Thanks @wangmiao0668000666, @davidcittadini, @LiuwqGit, @yetval, @masatohoshino, @YangManBOBO, @RomneyDa, @shanselman, @dor-sr, @cristianoc, and @brucemccurdy.
- **Operator control continuity:** native computer control recovers after session expiry, late-attached GitHub operators can publish PRs, synchronous node output is not duplicated as a completion wake, cron announcements preserve CLI chats, and history maintenance reads identities before payloads. (#169385, #169400, #164511, #176218, #174530) Thanks @stackingrockss, @Gigaxel, @holgergruenhagen, @eliavb43, @wangmiao0668000666, @asikorskiy, and @RomneyDa.
- **Provider and plugin continuity:** model refresh, configured-account readiness, GPT-5.6 tool turns, OpenRouter onboarding, incremental plugin loading, and faster external TypeScript plugin startup retain current state instead of rejecting valid setup or discarding providers. (#176709, #178522, #173366, #173292, #162226, #161267, #168391) Thanks @ericcaiwx-star, @eduardonunesfreire-rgb, @chandraveshchaudhari, @netcrazed, @obviyus, @jakeaadams, and @RomneyDa.
- **Managed integration reliability:** saved Linux Gateway dashboards preserve pairing across restarts, slow macOS Talk runs retain their replies, app upgrades converge official plugins, Copilot setup verifies SDK-backed agents correctly, Claude CLI cache prefixes stay stable after child completion and retain context when caller-only tools appear or disappear, and passkey prompts no longer block headless browser clicks. (#158908, #164485, #174257, #163578, #172026, #178955, #170857) Thanks @dor-sr, @PollyBot13, @kazuyuki-eguchi, @lifuyue, @Marvinthebored, @VACInc, @trukhinyuri, @Peetiegonzalez, @RomneyDa, @shanselman, @wangmiao0668000666, @brucemccurdy, and @rsaeks.
- **Cross-platform app-managed upgrades:** native state repair, recovery snapshots, Gateway runtime admission, and post-upgrade service recovery now converge without losing agent access across macOS and Windows. (#171508, #174297, #175007, #176174, #178155, #178779, #180010, #180576, #180769) Thanks @tjarrau-dev, @DonnieFi, @jayzhou2309, @lostsock1, @sglion777, @Almost-Certified-ops, @billpang1-sketch, and @RomneyDa.

### Changes

- **Google models:** add Gemini 4 Argon support. (#171852) Thanks @RomneyDa.

### Fixes

- **Update guidance:** avoid irrelevant database-repair advice when a package manager is missing, and remove superseded warnings after a successful update. (#173293, #173395) Thanks @DonnieFi, @RomneyDa, @wangmiao0668000666, @sunlit-deng, and @bhedanikhilkumar-code.
- **macOS onboarding:** allow fresh profiles to start the Gateway and complete automatic setup. (#173246) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- **Gateway logging:** prevent a deleted or stale temporary log directory from wedging the Gateway at full CPU during date rollover. (#160433) Fixes #130807 Thanks @masatohoshino, @WadeOwenWatts, and @RomneyDa.
- **Control UI queue state:** clear slash-steer chips after the queued command is consumed. (#180024) Thanks @RomneyDa.

name: openclaw 2026.9.34
body:
This is a gateway-only `extended-stable` release, which is our current equivalent to LTS. This release is OpenClaw from the end of September 2026, plus critical security updates, reliability and performance fixes, and features like new model support. The latest version of OpenClaw at the time of this release is [2026.10.6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases#release-v2026.10.6)

## 2026.9.34

### Highlights

- **Safer agent file edits:** `apply_patch` now validates an ordered envelope before mutating the workspace, so a later invalid hunk cannot delete files changed by an earlier operation. (#160409) Thanks @masatohoshino, @obviyus, and @RomneyDa.
- **More reliable managed upgrades:** app-owned updates now converge official plugins alongside core and retain repair diagnostics. Fixes #174120. (#174257) Thanks @kazuyuki-eguchi and @RomneyDa.
- **Memory Wiki data safety:** OKF concept re-imports now preserve human-authored notes. Fixes #175700. (#175707) Thanks @YangManBOBO and @RomneyDa.
- **Reliable model startup and selection:** Gateway startup now survives model-refresh ownership replacement, and catalog readiness honors the effective primary model's configured account pin. Fixes #178502. (#173366, #178522) Thanks @ericcaiwx-star, @eduardonunesfreire-rgb, and @RomneyDa.
- **Gateway and integration stability:** log rotation no longer spins on a deleted `/tmp`, Buzz relay closure no longer exits the Gateway during authentication, and OpenRouter onboarding accepts valid credentials. Fixes #147269. (#160433, #170591, #173292) Thanks @masatohoshino, @jarvis-modern-mail, @chandraveshchaudhari, @RomneyDa, and @WadeOwenWatts.
- **Plugin hooks restored:** `before_tool_call` hooks now run under `openclaw agent exec`. Fixes #158824. (#159333) Thanks @joseairosa and @RomneyDa.

### Changes

- **Managed update convergence:** official plugins are reconciled to the app-managed core version during upgrades, with diagnostics retained for repair paths. Fixes #174120. (#174257) Thanks @kazuyuki-eguchi and @RomneyDa.

### Fixes

- **Agent patch atomicity:** preflight ordered `apply_patch` envelopes before mutation so later invalid hunks cannot destroy earlier files. (#160409) Thanks @masatohoshino, @obviyus, and @RomneyDa.
- **Memory Wiki note preservation:** retain human-authored notes when OKF concepts are imported again. Fixes #175700. (#175707) Thanks @YangManBOBO and @RomneyDa.
- **Model lifecycle and auth selection:** keep startup alive through model-refresh replacement and honor the configured primary account pin during catalog readiness. Fixes #178502. (#173366, #178522) Thanks @ericcaiwx-star, @eduardonunesfreire-rgb, and @RomneyDa.
- **Gateway logging and Buzz stability:** avoid deleted-log-target CPU spin and prevent NIP-42 relay closure from exiting the Gateway. Fixes #147269. (#160433, #170591) Thanks @masatohoshino, @jarvis-modern-mail, @RomneyDa, and @WadeOwenWatts.
- **OpenRouter onboarding:** accept valid API keys during route verification. (#173292) Thanks @chandraveshchaudhari and @RomneyDa.
- **Agent plugin hooks:** restore `before_tool_call` execution for `openclaw agent exec`. Fixes #158824. (#159333) Thanks @joseairosa and @RomneyDa.
- **Cross-release updater compatibility:** retain the 2026.10.1 launchd observation and updater runtime exports during extended-stable replacement, and conservatively refuse immutable-install mutation on this older release line. (#160663) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- **Patched Node runtime floors:** require Node `>=24.22.1 <25 || >=26.12.1` across install, update, Docker images, and the macOS app runtime check, so upgrades refuse vulnerable runtimes with a clear next step. (#181073) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- **Dependency advisories:** patch `zod` (GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5), `body-parser`, and other production advisories on this release line. (#181341) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- **Session durability:** skip empty transcript archive materialization and fence the first creation during transcript reconciliation. (#170122) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- **Claude CLI session continuity:** subagent completions no longer reset the Claude CLI session and lose prior context. (#178955) Thanks @Marvinthebored and @RomneyDa.
- **Update recovery:** complete interrupted update recovery safely and preserve admission interruption reasons for Doctor follow-up. (#181503, #181870) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- **Backup, Linux, and macOS repairs:** carry backup and platform service repairs needed by this release line, including the legacy macOS Gateway status path. (#181466) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- **Release validation compatibility:** reconcile branch-native update admission, declaration surfaces, safety baselines, and test fixtures required by the current full-release validation toolchain. (#180988) Thanks @RomneyDa.

### Complete contribution record

The expanded maintenance audit covers all 743 selected source rows from the
2026.10 stable and beta release lines after `v2026.9.33`: 596 unique numbered
PRs and 105 unnumbered release companions. The final source-row dispositions
are 142 applied, 82 branch-adapted, 128 already covered, and 391 explicitly
excluded.

The complete deduplicated PR inventory, mixed source-row sequences, unnumbered
companions, and exclusion reasons are preserved in the
[2026.9.34 extended-stable backport audit](../docs/releases/2026.9.34-backport-audit.md).
The grouped notes above remain the user-impact summary rather than repeating
the hundreds-row audit.
