name: OpenWork v0.18.62
body:
## Work with OneDrive and SharePoint files in OpenWork

- **Work with OneDrive and SharePoint files.** Agents can search, open, edit, and save Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files, including files shared with you, once an admin enables the required permission.
- **Workbot's Browser and Computer views connect again.** If a computer needs an update, Workbot rebuilds it when you open the view; it avoids rebuilding while a task is running.
- **Sign-in and connected admin tools are safer.** The desktop app now blocks unsafe non-web links from remote MCP sign-in requests. For teams connecting OpenWork to other AI tools, Den admin changes require write access, scripts cannot call admin tools, and credential data cannot be read through `den_query`.
- **For admins and self-hosters: Den gets security and recovery fixes.** Self-hosted Den deployments should update for recent Next.js security fixes, and opt-in administrator permission recovery now works with common database encodings. Operators can also enable hashed sign-in session tokens without signing anyone out.

Full changelog: https://openworklabs.com/docs/changelog · [Compare](https://github.com/different-ai/openwork/compare/v0.18.61...v0.18.62)

*Windows installers are signed using Microsoft Artifact Signing.*

name: OpenWork v0.18.61
body:
## Keep agent work in view while you work elsewhere

- **Keep agent work in view while you work elsewhere.** Desktop users can pop the computer view and floating browser into their own windows above other apps, and browser full screen now fills the display.
- **Dictate messages and use workspace commands again.** On macOS and Windows, dictation shows your words as you speak, stops when you click the mic again, and keeps words across pauses. On OpenCode v2, `/` lists workspace commands and skills, and picking one runs it.
- **Follow Workbot's browser work and longer tasks.** Workbot shows browser activity live and links to pages it opened. Background tasks can pass files and read just the part they need, while longer scripts and documents can finish without a cut-off reply being mistaken for completed work.
- **Invitations and connections take clearer paths.** Invited teammates can join their workspace during sign-in, invitation emails explain who invited them and where to get help, and completed MCP sign-ins no longer appear to fail. Teams messages and Outlook meeting invitations now wait for your confirmation.
- **For admins: organization and billing details are clearer.** Compact organization rows, recent organizations, and week-over-week summaries make admin pages easier to scan. The Free plan covers up to five users, and pending invitations count until they expire.
- **For self-hosters: web access and standalone installs are more predictable.** `openwork-server web` answers only its own host names unless you add proxy names with `--allowed-hosts`. Standalone server and bootstrap installs require Node.js 24.x (24.22.1 or newer), and the bootstrap installer downloads a supported runtime when needed.

Full changelog: https://openworklabs.com/docs/changelog · [Compare](https://github.com/different-ai/openwork/compare/v0.18.60...v0.18.61)

*Windows installers are signed using Microsoft Artifact Signing.*

name: v5.1.45
body:
**Reading the end of a long session takes 42 ms and 68 MB instead of 40 s and 1.8 GB.** `session_read`, `session_search` and `session_info` page through OpenCode's message API instead of loading the whole session: on a 23,000-message session, `session_read` with `limit: 2, from_end: true` dropped from 39.6 s and 1,848 MB peak memory to 42 ms and 68 MB, and a search that runs out its 60-second timeout now stops reading when it returns, where it used to read another 228 MB in the background ([#10738](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10738), [#10741](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10741)).

**OmO's extension no longer carries an LSP engine it never runs.** The native LSP tools and post-edit diagnostics already go through the packaged LSP daemon, but the formatter's import pulled lsp-core's whole in-process engine into `omo.js`; importing only the helpers it uses shrinks the extension by about 82 KB, with no change in behavior. ([#10659](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10659))

**Every session start reads about 33 KB less of `omo.js`: eleven memory slash commands and memory sync's device account load on first use ([#10902](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10902), [#10860](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10860)).** The commands (`/memory`, `/remember`, `/init`, `/recompile`, `/memory-repository`, `/sleeptime`, `/reflect`, `/dream`, `/search`, `/facts`, `/agreements`) still appear at startup with the same names, descriptions and hints; their handlers load from `extensions/omo-memory-commands.js`. The signed-in device account loads from `extensions/omo-device-account.js` the first time a session resolves its sync, and if that file cannot load, memory sync reports `sync-unavailable` with the reason instead of looking signed out.

**ulw-research ships a fact ledger, a fidelity state file and a claim index for research reports.** They give each research run a machine-readable record of its facts and verified claims; nothing in the CLI uses them yet. ([#11046](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11046), part of [#11009](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/11009); batch [#11148](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11148))

**Child-task, workflow and workpool wake sources report kind `children`.** ([#11114](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11114), part of [#10782](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10782))

**An unreadable workpool store no longer drops or falsely clears the children wake source.** ([#11118](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11118), part of [#10782](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10782))

**The children wake source reads the workpool store once per snapshot.** ([#11124](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11124), part of [#10782](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10782)) (batch [#11148](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11148))

**Child results waiting in the wake queue keep the parent from reading as done.** ([#11115](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11115), part of [#10782](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10782))

**The wake-queue count can no longer cost a delivery receipt and is re-published per session generation.** ([#11121](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11121), part of [#10782](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10782))

**A receipt that throws no longer leaves the wake-queue count up.** ([#11122](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11122), part of [#10782](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10782))

**Delivery receipts are isolated from each other, on retire too, and no receipt error is dropped.** ([#11123](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11123), part of [#10782](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10782)) (batch [#11148](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11148))

**A wake-queue flush settles each receipt and the child count once, and a throwing `onReceiptError` no longer stops the rest.** ([#11137](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11137), part of [#10782](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10782)) (batch [#11148](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11148))

**Windows helper tree kills are guarded against recycled parent PIDs.** A QA helper no longer stops an unrelated process tree that reused a parent's PID. ([#11007](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11007))

**A task that a quitting session suspended says why it is still running.** Quitting the owning session parks every live child, but the parked record kept its bare `running` status with no reason, so a restart that never resumed that session read as a running task that nothing would ever move. The quit shutdown now records `session_quit` on the parked record, which `task_output` and the task snapshot present as "resuming (session quit)", and a later resume whose reconcile defers the revival replaces it with the deferral's own reason. ([senpi#3493](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/issues/3493), [#10533](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10533), thanks [@Bearmancer](https://github.com/Bearmancer))

**A project's skills can no longer reach outside the project, and their MCP servers no longer get your whole environment.** A skill link in a project that points outside it is refused, and the reason shows in the skill tool's result and in OpenCode; links into skill folders you configured yourself still work. MCP servers that come from a project's skills start with a small safe base (paths, home, temp, locale, CA paths) plus the variables they declare. When one asks for a variable it didn't get, the result names it with the exact `/omo-mcp-env-grant` command that saves the grant for that server declaration; only names are stored, in the same file the engine uses. Skills you installed yourself, including paths in your global OpenCode configuration, keep today's environment. Task discovery keeps nested reference documents out of skills and allows links between packages in the same repository. Unreadable or missing skills report their actual file error rather than a security block. Replaced or evicted grant commands expire, and reopening the server provides a fresh command when needed. ([#10716](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10716))

**Computer use explains a refused macOS launch context instead of reporting a closed engine.** Initial activation and later restarts now report `COMPUTER_LAUNCH_CONTEXT_REQUIRED` with recovery instructions when the actual engine child refuses to start. Permission errors, desktop handover, and the native launch gate keep their existing behavior. ([#11073](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/11073), [#11086](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11086))

**Thread tools check that an RPC host is the one they selected before changing a session ([#10712](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10712)).** The client proves the host's key with a challenge-response and attaches the selected session by its durable id on the same connection, so a host that reused a routing id cannot receive another session's mutation. A draining host answers with a retryable `host_draining` error instead of failing the call, and a change that took effect is never reported as failed.

**The build now records which files each bundled artifact is built from.** `packages/omo-senpi/bundle-inputs.json` lists every repo file the generators of the committed bundles read. The list is traced from the recipe itself, and CI checks that it is current. Merge tooling can now tell that a skill-only change leaves the bundles untouched ([#11079](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/11079), [#11084](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11084)).

**A session with telemetry off clears leftover session summaries as soon as it starts.** Summary files a crashed session left behind used to stay on disk until a later session with telemetry on picked them up. A session with telemetry off now deletes them at startup when `omo.json` turns telemetry off for their project; an opt-out set only through an environment variable such as `DO_NOT_TRACK` applies to that session alone and leaves other sessions' summaries in place. Turning telemetry off in `omo.json` takes effect on the very next turn instead of up to five seconds later. A summary whose project cannot be told apart is never sent. ([#10234](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10234)) ([#10267](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10267)) (batch [#11148](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11148))

**Session summaries survive a crash at any step and are never counted twice.** Each summary window now has its own id, sent as the event id, and is written to a local pending file before it is sent; the file is deleted only after delivery is confirmed, and a later OmO start re-sends anything left over under the same id. A window left open by a killed process is sent once, only after that process is gone and its once-a-minute heartbeat has stopped for 5 minutes, so a sleeping laptop keeps its own window. The session sequence survives restarts and counts within a random per-run `summary_epoch`, and a session continued or recovered by another process starts a new one, so two processes writing one session never send the same (epoch, sequence) pair even when one of them is wrongly taken for dead, costs are added as whole 1/10,000 USD units (`cost_1e4`) so summaries and raw turns agree exactly, and `dropped_events` counts what had to be discarded after 14 days. `telemetry.rawTurnSampleRate` (or `OMO_TELEMETRY_RAW_TURN_SAMPLE_RATE`) sets the share of sessions that also send raw turn rows, 0.05 by default. ([#10198](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10198), [#10225](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10225)) (batch [#11148](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11148))

**Every session event says whether it came from a session you opened or one OmO spawned.** `session_started`, `turn_completed` and `session_summary` carry `session_role` (`root`, `child` or `unknown`), so a delegated child's usage is not counted again on top of its parent. ([#10198](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10198), [#10225](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10225)) (batch [#11148](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11148))

**Raw turn rows keep the name of a public model reached through your own gateway.** `turn_completed` masked the model to `custom` whenever the provider was not one OmO ships, while `session_summary` and every other event already kept a published model id regardless of the routing provider. The gateway name itself is still never sent. ([#10198](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10198), [#10225](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10225)) (batch [#11148](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11148))

**Plan review keeps working after a restart or a restored session ([#10558](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10558)).** plan-consultant and plan-reviewer only spawn after you asked for ulw-plan and a plan file exists. That state used to live only in memory, so after a restart, a desktop restore or a resumed session the gate was empty and plan review was refused until you asked again. The gate is now rebuilt from the session's own transcript when it starts: plan file reads and writes count again, and a request counts only when the engine recorded you typed it (senpi 2026.10.21-2 and later), so text injected by an extension still never opens it. State handed over by a reload is kept as well (#10378).

**The engine moves to senpi 2026.10.23-1: scheduled prompts and `/loop` ticks reach an open session mid-turn, the footer shows what subagents spent, and compaction works again on very long sessions and turns ([#11126](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11126)).** A scheduled prompt now arrives in its open session, steered into the running turn when the agent is working, and a `/loop` tick that comes due mid-turn is read at the next step. Each session remembers the thinking level per model. Stop pauses the session until you type or `/resume`. An HTTP MCP server with no saved sign-in no longer freezes the process for up to 30 seconds, a background usage check no longer locks a healthy Claude login on a network error, and a `models.json` entry without a price keeps the built-in price instead of billing $0. The built-in `/llama` llama.cpp integration is removed upstream; a saved `llama.cpp` provider is ignored.

**Bun-installed `omo` keeps its command links intact so later upgrades can succeed.** Launches still start directly on Bun, and a new-version launch restores older generated wrappers to symlinks. This fixes recurring `EEXIST` failures on Bun 1.4.4; the first upgrade from an old wrapper may need the one-time removal described in the PR. ([#11024](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11024))

**The engine moves to senpi 2026.10.21-3: long 1M-context conversations stop re-writing their cached prefix, Anthropic subscription context is counted once, and "No credential slots available" no longer locks every account out ([#10965](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10965)).** When context reduction trims a long conversation on a 1M window, the reduced prefix now stays identical and keeps its cache checkpoint, so each step writes only what changed. Anthropic subscription turns with internal SDK re-requests no longer double the context percentage or start compaction early, and a configured compaction model now does threshold, speculative and idle compaction while your session provider is healthy. The subscription lane is the only layer that picks its accounts, so one revoked or briefly rate-limited account no longer blocks the rest until you log in again. Every turn end says what happens next, a turn-end report names the hold your queued message released, the trailing "Anything else? (optional)" card is gone from clients without native questions, and moving a session between machines runs through one implementation. Forced recovery after a context overflow no longer picks the same compaction cut again when an invisible entry leads the session; an overflow still never moves a task to its next fallback model.

**Tasks honour a `-fast` model alias that the provider config pairs with a model.** Kibitzer no longer stops at a model whose start is refused; it falls back to the next one. ([#10538](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10538), fixes [#10536](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10536))

**Child startup failures keep their cause.** When a task child exits while the parent writes to stdin, its own typed failure is reported instead of a broken-pipe error. ([#11097](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11097), fixes [#11096](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/11096))

**The side panel says, once, that its column needs the fullscreen TUI.** `side_panel.enabled` renders its right-hand column only in the fullscreen TUI (`--tui-mode fullscreen`, or `tuiMode` in senpi's settings); in the default regular mode the sections stay a block above the editor. The docs now say so at the top of the `side_panel` table, and the first regular-mode run with the panel on shows a one-time notice naming both ways to switch. ([#10560](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10560), [#10565](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10565))

**A background task that wakes itself up, or reconnects after the task host restarts, keeps the right finished/running mark on the host ([#11094](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11094)).** A task that started a new run on its own just as its previous turn finished could stay marked as finished, so a replaced task host might drop it while it was still working. A finished task whose host restarted could lose its finished mark, so the new host might reopen it. Both now keep the correct mark. ([#11092](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/11092))

**The side panel shows subscription usage when you are signed in but the engine is serving through an environment token ([#10564](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10564)).** It used to show nothing in that case; it still never shows a different signed-in account's numbers. ([#11101](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11101))

**The one-line Linux installer picks the glibc build on glibc hosts that also have the `musl` package installed.** `install.sh` used to treat any `/lib/ld-musl-*.so.1` loader as proof of a musl system, so Debian or Ubuntu hosts with `musl-tools` or `musl-dev` installed downloaded `omo-linux-x64-musl` and recorded it for later updates. A glibc host (one where `getconf GNU_LIBC_VERSION` answers) now always gets the glibc build. The musl check also reads `ldd --version` in a way that still matches under `pipefail`, since musl's `ldd` exits 1 after printing its version. ([#10562](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10562), [#10612](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10612))

**`bun run lint` runs the copy check again, and Bun no longer warns on every process in the repo.** The root `package.json` had two `"lint"` scripts after a merge, so the copy check was silently skipped and Bun printed a "Duplicate key" warning to stderr each time it started, which failed tests that expect a quiet child. One `lint` script now runs both checks, and a test rejects repeated keys in any `package.json`. ([#11108](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11108))

**Memory notes keep their exact line endings on Windows.** Git for Windows converts line endings by default, so a note committed with LF or mixed endings came back with CRLF in a reflection worktree, and the description preflight that must keep every non-description byte failed there. Every memory repository now pins `core.autocrlf=false`, and opening an older repository restores only the working copies whose sole difference from the committed note is the converted line endings. ([#11112](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11112), fixes [#11109](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/11109)) (batch [#11148](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11148))

**Memory reflection and dream runs trim oversized note descriptions before completion validation.** The note body is preserved, instead of the run failing again and again and parking the identity. ([#10999](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10999))

**The frontend skill now decides what a screen leaves out before drawing it, and visual QA proves a redesign improved and stops after a few rounds ([#11023](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11023)).** Before code, every screen names one primary action, its information priorities, what it leaves out on purpose, and the content it must keep; after the draft renders, a subtraction pass removes what the user does not need and checks nothing required was dropped or merged. Small changes now read the project's design file and at most one reference instead of the whole library, and atmosphere and award-grade styling are built only when the brief asks. Visual QA gains a before/after mode that captures fixed cases before the first edit and compares them side by side, and its review loop now ends after 2-3 rounds: layout, function, accessibility and missing-content defects earn another round, taste notes are recorded and stop it.

**Computer use refuses input while the stop chord cannot be heard.** On macOS, a password field or Secure Keyboard Entry turns on Secure Event Input, which hides key presses from the stop chord's listener; computer use kept running anyway, so the chord could not stop it. Input is now refused with `StopPathUnavailable` (`secure-input-active`) until secure input ends, and resumes by itself. A `type` in progress now stops at the next character when the stop path stops authorizing input, instead of finishing the text, and the Linux X11 listener refuses to arm on an XInput 2.0 server, where a keyboard grab would swallow the chord. Plain Esc stays an ordinary key. ([#10534](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10534), [#9651](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/9651), [#10537](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10537))

**The frontend draft guard now catches promotional copy, emoji icons, hype badges and vanity stats, not only accent stripes ([#11022](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11022)).** One command, `check-draft-guard.ts`, runs the accent-stripe rules plus four checks on visible markup text: promotional filler in English and Korean copy, an emoji used as an icon, a badge whose only content is a hype label such as "New" or "AI-powered", and a stat tile holding a marketing-form number such as "10x", "500+" or "24/7"; a measured figure such as "42%" or "1.2k" passes. Code (TypeScript generics and comparisons included), scripts, styles, comments, hidden elements, bound values and badges that carry a state attribute are not flagged. React component tags such as `<Badge>` and `<Stat value="10x">`, `cn()` class lists, and announced attributes such as `aria-label` and `placeholder` are checked too. The frontend and visualize skills now run it before visual QA in place of `check-accent-stripes.ts`, which still works on its own. Both commands now skip a dangling symlink in a scanned folder instead of crashing, and report an unreadable path given on the command line with exit 2.

**A memory sync that stops working now says so in the TUI, with what to do.** When a sync cycle failed, the error went only to the log, and the status kept reporting the last successful sync. Now the memory footer shows `sync blocked` while sync is failing, and one notice says why and what to do: `/memory unlock <path>` for a git lock left behind by a crashed writer, sign in again for an expired sign-in, or check your connection when the sync service cannot be reached. A single dropped request still retries quietly; the offline notice appears only after three failed cycles in a row. When sync recovers, a notice says so and the footer clears. ([#10637](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10637), [#10958](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10958))

**Store extensions can expose session-callable ops as real tools, and their worker no longer drags a schema library into every store.** A store extension's `sessionCallable` declaration can now carry a `toolName`, `description` and JSON Schema `parameters` per op: the session's engine registers it as `ext_<extension>_<toolName>`, the tool takes the calling session's durable id from the engine (never from arguments), and the worker stamps `caller_session_durable_id` and, when the caller thread_create'd the target, `caller_created_target` inside the op's own transaction. Args naming either caller field are refused before validation; the public `extensionCall` channel refuses every declared session op. The worker validates op arguments itself against a JSON Schema subset (`type`, `properties`, `required`, `additionalProperties` true/false, `enum`, `const`, `pattern`, length/item/number bounds, `items`, `anyOf`), and `register()` refuses any other keyword, so no constraint is skipped - which also removed typebox/value from the store worker: its bundle drops from 206 KB to 115 KB and every worker spawn (and idle-retire respawn) stops paying for its module graph. A declared `await` with `statusOp`/`expireOp`/`timeoutMs` arms a wake-file wait, and `thread_creations` records who created which session durably across host restarts. ([#9551](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/9551))

**Product copy uses clearer punctuation instead of em dashes ([#10994](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10994)).** Agent prompts, notices, memory recall openers, and web metadata now use commas, colons, or parentheses, and an empty-value placeholder uses a hyphen. A source AST check prevents new em dashes in product strings, template elements, and JSX text while leaving comments, regexes, tests, generated code, and vendored sources alone. The same check now requires lint and TypeScript suppressions to explain why, inline or in the comment directly above, including Biome ignores.

**Inside OmO Desktop the browser skill works as in the terminal, plus the app's built-in browser.** The agent's browsers (your own through BrowserSkill, or one it starts itself) are no longer refused or changed inside the app, and `connectBuiltinBrowser()` adds the thread's tab in the app's built-in browser, which you can watch beside the chat ([#11066](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11066)).

**A session in the OmO desktop app's Built-in browser mode can ask the app for its in-app browser.** The browser skill told the agent to use the app's in-app browser tools, but an OmO session had none, so agents reached for whatever outside browser the machine had (sisyphuslabs/omo-desktop-app#3292). A new eval-only `omo_desktop_toolkit` tool asks the app for a toolkit it hosts for the session's thread, and `connectBuiltinBrowser()` in the browser skill uses it to attach OmOWright to that thread's tab. The app's grant names a loopback endpoint and a token file, so the token never appears in a tool result; an app that offers no toolkit is answered at once, and one that does not answer within 15 s gets a timeout. Works once the desktop app ships its side. ([#10602](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10602), fixes [#10601](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10601))

**Parked facts leave the active queue without losing their contents.** Existing backlogs migrate once, manual retry restores them, and turn-end scans read only active entries. ([#11038](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11038))

**The side panel's usage section reads the subscription limits the engine already keeps, so it shows the same numbers as the desktop, before the first turn, and makes no network request of its own ([#10553](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10553)).** senpi now polls each signed-in Claude and ChatGPT subscription itself ([code-yeongyu/senpi#3687](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/pull/3687)); the panel only picks the serving account and draws its record. A rotation to an account the engine has not read yet shows nothing rather than the previous account's numbers. `side_panel.usage_poll_seconds` is retired: still accepted, now ignored.

**A finished background task no longer wakes up on its own after the task host restarts ([#11083](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11083)).** A task that ran on the shared task host kept its session loaded there after it finished, with nothing saying it was done. When the host was replaced, the new host reopened it, and the task's own follow-ups could run again with nobody watching, spending usage. The task now marks its session as finished on the host as soon as it finishes, and again before it lets go, so the new host leaves it closed even if the parent session crashed. A finished task you continue with `task_send` is marked running again before your message is delivered; a dropped connection that reconnects does not change the mark. ([#10778](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10778))

**The web-terminal visual QA driver can wait for text before it types.** A slow-starting TUI used to lose its first keystrokes to the fixed start delay. Put `{WaitFor:<text>}` in `--input` and the driver polls the rendered xterm buffer until `<text>` appears, then continues; if it never appears within `--wait-for-timeout-ms` (default 10000) the capture fails with an error naming the text and the timeout, and an empty `{WaitFor:}` is refused. Thanks to @cynkai. ([#9583](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/9583), [#9666](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/9666))

**git-master credits sisyphus-dev-ai on its commits again, once per commit, and you can turn it off.** Every commit git-master writes ends with `Co-authored-by: sisyphus-dev-ai <sisyphus-dev-ai@users.noreply.github.com>`. Git adds the trailer itself (`git -c trailer.ifexists=addIfDifferent commit --trailer`), so amending or rewording a commit that already carries it keeps a single copy, and after a squash git-master rewrites the joined message once. This needs git 2.32 or newer. `git_master.include_co_authored_by` in `omo.json` is a working switch again and defaults to `true`; set it to `false` to leave the trailer out. The commit footer stays opt-in, your own git author and committer are unchanged, and the `GIT_MASTER=1` prefix applies to the commit command as before. This works the same in the Native harness (reading the skill or `load_skills`) and the OpenCode plugin ([#10713](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10713), [#10715](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10715)).

**The count of undelivered messages matches the messages actually dropped ([#10987](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10987)).** When a stopped parent cancelled a task, or a task that could not be resumed was closed, its queued messages were dropped with a note saying how many. That count came from a read taken just before the queue was cleared, so a message sent in between was dropped without being counted. The count now comes from the same write that clears the queue. ([#10866](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10866))

**A relaunched task records its own session id, not the previous run's ([#10985](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10985)).** When a task restarted on a new transcript (a model fallback or a revive) and its new session's first state read failed, the task kept the previous run's session id, so anything that looks a task up by its session id, such as the task tree or the cleanup when a parent stops, found the old session. The first id the new run learns now replaces it. ([#10892](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10892))

**The footer shows what your subagents are spending, live, next to the session's own cost ([#10730](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10730)).** The session cost only counted the session itself, so the number stood still while subagents worked. The footer now adds the whole subagent tree's spend as `(+$X)`, including nested children and revived runs, and updates as tasks report instead of polling ([code-yeongyu/senpi#2471](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/issues/2471)).

**Subagent rows no longer show `$0.0000` when the provider sent no usage ([#10727](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10727)).** A turn whose provider streamed no usage block came back with an all-zero usage, and the task row counted it as a real $0, with no tok/s. Such a turn now counts as "cost not reported", so the row shows no amount, and a run where only some turns reported a cost is marked `partial` ([#10724](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10724)).

**Internal: a telemetry spool lock this process could not delete no longer blocks its batch until the 14-day age limit.** After a transient file error (for example on Windows), the sweep reclaims the lock once the claim lease has passed, while a lock for a move still in progress is kept ([#10951](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10951)).

**Internal: every assistant turn opens one `omo.turn` OpenTelemetry span, and events emitted during the turn carry its trace and span ids.** On a transport with a span sink (the OTLP collector transport; the PostHog transport has none) the Senpi adapter starts the span at `turn_start` and ends it `ok`, or `error` for a failed or abandoned turn, so a `turn_completed` row, its span and an error event join on the (`trace_id`, `span_id`) pair. A process child launched by the task engine continues the delegating turn's trace. The `traceparent` header goes only to our own hosts, never to a model provider, and nothing is started or written while telemetry is off. ([#10358](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10358))

**Internal: the telemetry spool recovers and bounds itself on every sweep, and a stalled sender never re-sends a batch it lost.** Every live collector transport sweeps the spool on start and every 60 s: it recovers expired claims and the files of dead processes, applies the 5 MB cap to everything in the directory (not only to what it sealed itself), and replays oldest first; when consent has ended the sweep deletes the spool instead. Before every send attempt the sender renames its claim to a fresh lease, so a process that stalled past its lease and lost the batch to another process stops instead of sending it again, and a batch claimed when consent is withdrawn is deleted unsent. Nothing is wired to a product yet. ([#10355](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10355))

**The engine publishes its OpenTelemetry schema artifact.** `telemetry-schema.json` describes exactly what an OTel client of the engine may send, generated from the event schemas and kept byte-exact by a drift gate, so the telemetry collector can pin and enforce it. It is separate from the anonymous PostHog events, which are unchanged ([#10980](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10980)).

**The frontend skill picks a layout pattern for every layout change, and visual-qa checks it.** Any change to a screen's structure (a new region, panel, split, list, sticky bar or scroll container) now fetches the matching StyleGallery pattern and writes one `Layout:` line in `DESIGN.md` naming the pattern, the element that owns the scroll and the pattern's anti-patterns, including in a project that already has a `DESIGN.md`. visual-qa's new A12 item checks the build against that line, with a probe for the element that really scrolls. Apple HIG hit targets, hierarchy, states, keyboard and motion are now rules for the first draft in the frontend skill, not only items in the QA checklist. ([#10684](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10684), [#10685](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10685))

**New TypeScript and JavaScript projects default to oxlint and oxfmt.** The programming skill now ships strict OXC configs and the t3code copy rules: product strings, templates, and JSX reject em dashes, and lint/type suppressions require an explanation. Existing repository toolchains are respected. ([#11030](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11030))

**Account commands no longer repeat a failed keychain operation while reporting the error.** A native storage failure or timeout now returns exit 9 with `{"error":"store-unavailable"}` instead of attempting another store read, which could add a second 25-second wait. Existing success and locked-keychain outcomes are preserved; no new deadline or lock change is introduced ([#11040](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/11040), [#11049](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11049)).

**A removed device ends its local account session on refresh.** When the service refuses a renewal with `device_revoked`, `omo account token` clears the saved credential and returns exit 5 with that code; `omo account show` then reports signed out. Unknown refusal codes still retain the credential as uncertain ([#11041](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/11041), [#11048](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11048)).

**Project memory reads work on Windows when a path uses a short user-directory name.** Read grants now compare native canonical paths on both sides, accounting for Windows case and separator differences without granting sibling memory repositories. A granted repository that is later replaced by a link elsewhere is no longer covered, and a note that does not exist yet is still allowed so the read can report it missing. ([#10982](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10982))

**Each model family's current default is named once.** Every builtin default, fallback rung, category gate, Claude Code alias and migration target that means "the newest Opus / Sonnet / Haiku / Fable / GPT / GLM / Kimi / Gemini" now reads its id from one table, so the next model bump is one edit. Resolved models stay the same, with one exception: the Claude Code `sonnet` alias now means the current Sonnet (`claude-sonnet-5-5`) instead of `claude-sonnet-4-6`. ([#10483](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10483), [#10141](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10141))

**A builtin model profile can run on your own provider.** When the only provider serving a profile's model is one you declared in `models.json` (for example an API-key proxy serving `claude-opus-5-5`), Daily · Normal and the other builtin lanes now pick it instead of reporting that no model is available. Only the models you declared for that provider count, the lane's own providers still come first, and gateways you never declared still never serve a builtin lane. Reported by 채완. ([#10493](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10493), [#10485](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10485))

**`/mass-ulw` and `run mass ulw ...` now enter the mode instead of offering a pointer the model could skip.** The slash command (`/mass-ulw`, `/mulw`, `/ulw-research`) or a prompt that starts with `run`, `start`, `use`, `do` or `execute` followed by the keyword (`run mass ulw research on <link>`; in Korean, `mass ulw 돌려줘` or `실행해줘`) now carries a binding instruction: read the skill before any other tool call, and run mass-ulw as workflow runs. Before, the hint asked the model to decide whether you meant it, and in a real run it skipped mass-ulw and started no workflow. Any other mention, including a prompt that only ends with `mass ulw research` or asks a question, still gets the hint, and quoted, relayed, negated and delegated mentions never arm it. A single-quoted name (`'omo-senpi ultrawork ...'`) and a relay header naming several recipients (`[a -> b + c]`) now count as quotes and relays for `ulw` too, so they no longer arm ultrawork ([#10810](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10810), [#10822](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10822)).

**A session can consult the memory of a project it touches.** The first successful read, edit or write under a child project with existing memory lists its note paths and descriptions, without injecting note bodies. Linked projects in a non-git workspace and linked worktrees follow the session's `auto_identity` mode. Kibitzer ranks up to three recently touched projects separately from the session's own notes, reserves up to half its seats for them, and uses the same persisted search-term cache for each repository. Project notes receive read-only grants; their `system/` tree, git metadata, writes and enumeration remain denied. Both `memory.project_scope.nudge` and `.recall` default to `true` and can be disabled separately. ([#10044](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10044), [#10921](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10921))

**omo.json can say which workspace a session belongs to ([#10852](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10852)).** `provenance.workspaces` lists workspaces by name with optional `git_owners` and `paths`; messages between sessions use it to show where the sender works (#10794).

**Messages between sessions start with the sender's workspace and project ([#10853](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10853), [#10794](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10794)).** The sender's environment, git owner or configured paths decide it, never the message text; older stored messages say provenance was not recorded (#10794).

**A memory git command that hangs past its timeout can now leave evidence behind.** With `OMO_GIT_TIMEOUT_DIAGNOSTICS_DIR` set, a timed-out git records the running process table (and on Windows the stuck git's thread wait states) in that directory before it is stopped; unset, nothing changes. Windows CI uses it to diagnose a rare stalled `git add`. ([#10821](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10821), [#10914](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10914))

**Stopping a task no longer risks matching a task with the same id from another task store ([#10903](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10903)).** When a task's session shuts down, it finds its own task by the task id in its session context. Task ids are unique only within one task store, so that id is now trusted only when the session's state folder is exactly this store's folder for that task; otherwise the session falls back to matching by its session id. ([#10881](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10881))

**Anonymous usage stats now count each person once.** The anonymous id is kept once per user instead of per agent directory, so runs that use their own agent directory, and the CLI next to OmO Desktop, no longer show up as separate people; runs in CI, under a test runner, or with a temporary home directory send nothing by default (`OMO_TELEMETRY_ALLOW_AUTOMATION=1` opts back in). This also holds on Windows: a temporary home folder there is recognised too, a home folder that cannot be found turns usage stats off rather than on, and a real profile under the users folder is never treated as temporary. On some machines the anonymous id changes once with this update ([#10935](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10935)).

**Refused child tasks report startup failure without waiting for slow teardown.** Shutdown still waits for pending cleanup ([#10988](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10988), fixes [#10402](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10402)).

### Fixed

- Memory facts extraction no longer loops until its deadline when a model fills the optional `person` field on a project fact with an empty placeholder: the placeholder is dropped and the fact is recorded, while a project fact naming a real person is still refused. A model that resends a refused `record_fact` call unchanged now ends the run with the facts it already recorded, and a parked queue entry no longer holds back that conversation's later entries ([#10918](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10918)). ([#10924](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10924))

name: v1.9.3
body:
## Highlights

- Embedded runtimes can coexist in one process with independent network policies, including background maintenance and provider requests.
- Add SQLite/PostgreSQL schema equivalence checks, sharded CI tests, and a web production-build check.
- Consolidate provider error factories and timeout defaults, extract credential resolution, and add a provider scaffold with safe failure cleanup.
- Include Slack callback verification, the AllRatesToday provider, Gmail rate-limit recovery, and OAuth refusal-page improvements.

## Default behavior change: lazy catalog schemas

The standalone server now loads action schemas on demand by default, matching the embedded runtime. Action metadata stays in memory; schemas are read from catalog files when needed. This reduces startup work and resident memory without changing API response content.

The first access to an uncached provider schema performs a file read, so keep the catalog files available throughout the runtime's lifetime. To restore the previous eager-loading behavior, set `OOMOL_CONNECT_CATALOG_LAZY_SCHEMAS=false`; embedded hosts can use `lazySchemas: false`.

## What's Changed
* feat(slackbot): add inbound event verification endpoint by @LM20230311 in https://github.com/oomol-lab/open-connector/pull/774
* fix(providers): report upstream rate limits as rate_limited by @Tong-bit-art in https://github.com/oomol-lab/open-connector/pull/775

name: career-ops v1.38.0: Five Thousand Strong
body:
<!-- co:release-notes:career-ops-v1.38.0 -->
This release is about not losing what you put in. Your CV, your PDF, your `portals.yml`, your tracker rows and your saved answers now survive interrupted writes, odd formatting and updates, and it comes from 48 people in one week, in the same days the career-ops Discord passed 5,000 members.

## Highlights

- **Updates that keep your files safe.** The list of what the updater owns now lives in its own manifest, read without importing, and an install on 1.37.0 updates through a bridge list. Tested before release from 1.37.0 and older installs: apply and rollback left the user files we checked byte-identical. (#5563 by @vliggio)
- **Writes that cannot half-happen.** `cv.md`, `portals.yml` and the generated PDF are replaced atomically, and every core lock now uses one protocol. (#5552, #5389 by @vliggio)
- **Batch, more in your hands.** `--company` limits a run to the companies you name, `--thin-action` decides what happens when no JD text could be fetched, and workers apply your dealbreakers and record a finished SKIP. (#5526, #5547 by @zhangruyi1993, #5493 by @mbrow190)
- **More places to look.** Computrabajo and Magneto365 for Latin America (#2650 by @configurowebmax), Atlassian (#5497 by @kellymmcgrath), Dover (#5565 by @IaroslavMazur), Zoho Recruit career sites (#5345 by @ilyakanevskiy) and white-label SuccessFactors sites in `scan:full` (#5740 by @Schlaflied).
- **Following up, with less to remember.** A duplicate check before you write a CV (#5735), take-home deadlines (#5736), interview invites read from an `.ics` file (#5744), all by @Schlaflied, and `tracker.mjs query --csv` for your spreadsheet (#5624 by @mbrow190).

### Security

- The web app's assisted apply could submit an application form when the text it typed contained a line break: line breaks are now removed from that text, and the fallback inserts it without pressing keys, so it no longer submits the form (GHSA-rm8h-2825-ww26, reported by @vliggio, #5770).

## Updating

Run `node update-system.mjs apply --confirm` in your career-ops folder. If you said no to the update prompt earlier, this is the same command.

### Thank you

This release carries 300 pull requests from 48 people, 17 of them contributing for the first time.

name: v15.0.2 — Stop observer reasoning from consuming the output budget
body:
# Stop observer reasoning from consuming the output budget

Observer requests to OpenRouter, the cmem.ai gateway, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints now disable reasoning by default, so reasoning tokens no longer fill the output budget and leave a session with zero observations.

- An empty reply with finish_reason=length is logged and retried once with reasoning forced off. That retry counts against the existing paid-send budget and is bounded by the per-attempt timeout.
- Billed usage keeps the retry's prompt size and adds completion tokens and cost from both attempts.
- Health status names the active OpenRouter credential, including a custom OPENROUTER_BASE_URL.
- OpenAI "Unsupported parameter" responses drop the reasoning field and remember the endpoint. Mandatory-reasoning and invalid-effort refusals are left in place.
- Empty replies that finish with stop stay accepted.

Ships the observer repair from #5029.

name: supervision-0.31.2
body:
# v0.31.2 — Pascal VOC boxes that match the devkit

A bug-fix release: Pascal VOC boxes now follow the devkit convention, and a batch of crashes on edge-case inputs is gone.

- **Pascal VOC** export and import use the devkit's box indices, so Detectron2 and other readers see the boxes you wrote.
- Gemini 2.5 and 3.5 masks survive boxes that leave the 0-1000 range instead of failing the whole response.
- Crop and icon annotators draw on grayscale scenes.
- Half-precision box centers stay finite instead of turning into `inf`.
- JSON sinks, dataset exports and the video reader stop losing data when something goes wrong.

Drop-in upgrade, with one catch: box-only Pascal VOC objects written by earlier versions now load one pixel larger on the right and bottom edges. The migration guide below shows how to fix them.

## ✨ Spotlights / highlights

### Pascal VOC boxes follow the devkit

`DetectionDataset.as_pascal_voc` and `from_pascal_voc` now treat `<bndbox>` indices as 1-based and inclusive, shifting only `xmin` and `ymin` by one, which is what Detectron2 and other devkit readers expect. Export also rounds corners to the nearest pixel instead of truncating them, so a YOLO box that `from_yolo` loads with float noise no longer grows a pixel. Box-only objects written by 0.31.1 and earlier carry an extra +1 in `xmax` and `ymax`; objects exported from masks already used the devkit maxima. (#2748, #2780)

```python
# `dataset` holds one box [10, 20, 40, 60]
dataset.as_pascal_voc(
    images_directory_path="images", annotations_directory_path="annotations"
)
# <bndbox>: xmin=11 ymin=21 xmax=40 ymax=60  (0.31.1: xmax=41 ymax=61)
# a YOLO box loaded as [0, 0, 37.0000001, 29.0000001]: 1 1 37 29  (0.31.1: 1 1 38 30)
```

### Gemini masks survive boxes outside the 0-1000 range

`Detections.from_vlm` with `VLM.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5` or `VLM.GOOGLE_GEMINI_3_5` raised `ValueError` as soon as a `box_2d` coordinate went above 1000 or below 0, even by one, and you lost every detection in the response. The mask is now cropped to the part of its box inside the image, a box wholly outside gets an all-false mask, and boxes inside the image produce the same masks as before. (#2793)

```python
import supervision as sv

# one item: {"box_2d": [500, 500, 1001, 1001], "label": "cat", "mask": "data:image/png;base64,..."}
detections = sv.Detections.from_vlm(
    sv.VLM.GOOGLE_GEMINI_3_5, result, resolution_wh=(1000, 800)
)
detections.mask.shape, int(detections.mask.sum())
# ((1, 800, 1000), 200000)
# 0.31.1: ValueError: could not broadcast input array from shape (400,501) into shape (400,500)
```

### Crop and icon annotators on grayscale scenes

`CropAnnotator` and `IconAnnotator` used to raise `IndexError` or `ValueError` on scenes shaped `(H, W)` or `(H, W, 1)`, or given as a Pillow `"L"` image. Crops now keep the scene's channel layout, and icons are drawn as their gray luminance, blended by their alpha channel. (#2788)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

scene = np.zeros((100, 100), dtype=np.uint8)
scene[20:60, 20:60] = 200
detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[20, 20, 60, 60]], dtype=float), class_id=np.array([0])
)
sv.CropAnnotator().annotate(scene.copy(), detections).shape
# (100, 100)  (0.31.1: IndexError: tuple index out of range)
```

### Half-precision boxes that stay finite

`sv.scale_boxes` and `Detections.get_anchors_coordinates` now compute box centers without overflowing `float16`: a box from 40000 to 60000 used to report an `inf` center. `DetectionsSmoother` also compares oriented-box corner distances in `float64`, which stops `float16` and narrow integer coordinates from overflowing; integer coordinates beyond `2**53` still lose low-order pixels in the `float64` average. (#2787, #2785)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[40000, 40000, 60000, 60000]], dtype=np.float16)
)
detections.get_anchors_coordinates(sv.Position.CENTER).tolist()
# [[49984.0, 49984.0]]  (0.31.1: [[inf, inf]])
```

## 🔄 Migration guide

One behavior change needs your attention: the Pascal VOC box convention. No public symbol was added, renamed or removed in this release, and nothing is deprecated.

**Pascal VOC `<bndbox>` indices** affects `sv.DetectionDataset.as_pascal_voc` and `sv.DetectionDataset.from_pascal_voc`. Before 0.31.2, export added 1 to all four corners of a box-only object and truncated, and import subtracted 1 from all four. From 0.31.2, both follow the devkit's 1-based, inclusive indices: only `xmin` and `ymin` are shifted by one, and export rounds to the nearest pixel. Export rounds every corner to a whole pixel and the loader returns `float32` coordinates, so check precision-sensitive boxes after a round trip. Files from different versions don't round-trip. (#2748, #2780)

| Box `[10, 20, 40, 60]` | Written `<bndbox>`                | Read back by 0.31.2 |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| written by 0.31.1      | `xmin=11 ymin=21 xmax=41 ymax=61` | `[10, 20, 41, 61]`  |
| written by 0.31.2      | `xmin=11 ymin=21 xmax=40 ymax=60` | `[10, 20, 40, 60]`  |

- Box-only objects (no `<polygon>`) in files written by 0.31.1 or earlier now load one pixel larger on the right and bottom edges. To restore the original boxes, subtract 1 from `<xmax>` and `<ymax>` of those objects only, or re-export the dataset from its source with 0.31.2. Objects exported from masks, which carry a `<polygon>`, already used the devkit maxima, so leave their files alone: their masks load as before, while their boxes now end one pixel further right and down.
- Files exported by 0.31.2 match what Detectron2 and other devkit readers expect, so workarounds for the old extra +1 in `xmax` and `ymax` can go.

## 📝 Notable changes

### ⚠️ Breaking Changes

- **Pascal VOC box extents** — `as_pascal_voc` and `from_pascal_voc` follow the devkit's 1-based, inclusive `<bndbox>` indices and export rounds corners to the nearest pixel. Box-only objects written by earlier versions load one pixel larger on the right and bottom edges, so check the migration guide before reading old VOC datasets. (#2748, #2780)

### 🔧 Fixed

**Datasets and file I/O**

- Dataset exports finished without an error even when an image could not be written, leaving image files missing; detection dataset exports and `ClassificationDataset.as_folder_structure` now raise `OSError` with the destination path. (#2772)
- `JSONSink.write_and_close()` raised `ValueError: I/O operation on closed file.` when called inside a `with` block, because the block's exit calls it again; it's now a no-op once the file is closed, like `CSVSink.close()`. (#2771)
- `JSONSink.append` kept references to its input, so reusing NumPy buffers or editing nested metadata changed rows that were already appended; it now snapshots the data. (#2781)
- NumPy boolean scalars are now written as JSON booleans in JSON files. (#2783)

**Detections and VLM**

- `Detections.from_vlm` with the Gemini 2.5 and 3.5 connectors failed on any item whose `box_2d` left the 0-1000 range; its mask is now cropped to the image. (#2793)
- `Detections.select()` raised an indexing error on selected rows that share a scalar value in `data`; scalar NumPy values are now preserved. (#2769)
- `sv.mask_iou_batch` now treats `CompactMask` inputs like dense masks: mismatched image shapes raise `ValueError`, unsupported overlap metrics are rejected even when bounding-box pre-filtering finds no pair, and exact NMS thresholds make the same decision for both. (#2767)
- `sv.scale_boxes` and `Detections.get_anchors_coordinates` overflowed to `inf` for `float16` boxes with large coordinates. (#2787)
- `DetectionsSmoother` could overflow or tie on `float16` and large integer coordinates when aligning oriented-box corners; integer coordinates beyond `2**53` still lose low-order pixels in the `float64` average. (#2785)

**Annotators and video**

- `CropAnnotator` and `IconAnnotator` raised `IndexError` or `ValueError` on grayscale scenes. (#2788)
- `get_video_frames_generator` left its video capture open when range validation or the initial seek failed; it now releases the capture and logs any secondary release error without replacing the original error. (#2782)

## 🏆 Contributors

Welcome to our first-time contributors: 卢文彬, SHLOK SINGH, zurrll, Huashuo Lei, moyunliuyin, Wentao Tong and LEE, WEI-HONG!

- **Avanish Garg** (@avanish-garg) — kept Gemini 2.5 and 3.5 masks when a box leaves the 0-1000 range.
- **Mohammad Hijjawi** (@MohammadHijjawi97) — made `CropAnnotator` and `IconAnnotator` work on grayscale scenes.
- **卢文彬** (@lu123bing) — fixed `inf` box centers for half-precision boxes.
- **A Aswanth Raj** (@aswanth-07) — fixed overflow in `DetectionsSmoother` corner alignment.
- **Kaushik Reddy Lingireddy** (@Lingikaushikreddy) — rounded Pascal VOC corners instead of truncating them.
- **moyunliuyin** (@moyunliuyin) — aligned Pascal VOC export and import with the devkit's box extents.
- **Junghwan** (@shaun0927) — fixed `JSONSink.append` buffer reuse and released video captures when setup fails.
- **Huashuo Lei** (@wpyaoxueros) — fixed `Detections.select()` with scalar data.
- **Wentao Tong** (@tongwentao) — made dataset exports raise when an image cannot be written.
- **kevin** (@kevin9327) — fixed `JSONSink.write_and_close()` after the file is closed.
- **Devulapalli Naga Sri Vaishnavi** (@Vaishnavi220506) — aligned `CompactMask` IoU with the dense-mask contract.
- @zurrll — saved NumPy booleans as JSON booleans.
- **SHLOK SINGH** (@buildwithshlok) — added type checking to the annotators tests.
- **LEE, WEI-HONG** (@AuricTW) — added a `cross_product` doctest.
- **Jirka Borovec** (@Borda) — prepared the release.

*Automated contributions: Dependabot, Copilot, Claude, pre-commit.ci*

## What's Changed

name: graphify 0.9.95
body:
Twenty-one community pull requests. A security pass on install: the skill-install writes go through randomly-named temp files instead of predictable ones, so a pre-planted symlink can no longer redirect a write. Extraction: Python, Go, C++ and Rust explicit type aliases (and Rust `union` items) are extracted as type nodes so references resolve instead of minting sourceless stubs, each C# method overload gets its own node bound by argument count, and a package.json dependency's manifest entry links to the node that references it. Plus a one-root-per-repo tree on merged graphs, extended-length cache paths on Windows, and binary media no longer counted as text. The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts.

- Fix: **security** the skill install stages every write (version stamp, `SKILL.md`, references) through a randomly-named `mkstemp`/`mkdtemp` file created with `O_EXCL` and restrictive mode instead of a predictable `*.tmp` name, so a local attacker who pre-creates a symlink at that path can no longer redirect the write to clobber an arbitrary file; the final move stays atomic (#4513, thanks @Mahdifotohi).
- Fix: **python** an explicit module-level type alias (`X: TypeAlias = ...`, `type X = ...`, `NewType`) is extracted as a type node, so a field or parameter typed by the alias resolves to it instead of minting a sourceless stub; an implicit assignment, a local alias, or a re-export is left alone (#4578, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik).
- Fix: **go** a `type A = B` alias is extracted as a type node (tree-sitter parses it as a `type_alias`, not a `type_spec`), so references resolve to it; a re-export (`type Field = pkg.Field`) mints no node (#4579, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik).
- Fix: **cpp** a namespace-scope `using A = B;` or `typedef B A;` alias is extracted as a type node so references resolve; a member alias inside a class and a same-name re-export are excluded (#4580, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik).
- Fix: **rust** a `type` alias and a `union` item are extracted as type nodes (a union's fields reference their types like a struct), so references resolve instead of minting stubs; an impl-associated `type` is excluded (#4581, Refs #4285, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik; reported by @jonatasbcardio-boop).
- Fix: **csharp** each method overload gets its own node and source location instead of collapsing to one, and a call binds to the overload matching its argument count, across in-file, receiver-typed, bare-name cross-file, partial-class, and interface-dispatch resolution; a non-overloaded method keeps its id (#4584, #4591, thanks @Mpasha17; reported by @TerraVenil).
- Fix: **tree** `graphify export tree` on a merged multi-repo graph gives each repo its own root (keyed by the repo tag) instead of conflating same-path files from different repos; untagged nodes are not counted as a repo (#4524, #4525, thanks @AromalBiju1).
- Fix: **cache** AST cache entries are read and written through Windows extended-length (`\\?\`) paths, so a deep cache path over the 260-character limit no longer fails extraction with a `FileNotFoundError`; a no-op off Windows (#4542, thanks @omsenjalia).
- Fix: **detect** a binary media file (an image or audio/video) is no longer read and counted as text toward the corpus word total; an SVG stays counted as the XML text it is (#4548, thanks @kalkaran).
- Fix: **json_config** a `package.json` dependency's manifest entry links (`declares`) to the ref node that importing code resolves to, so the manifest entry and its importers share one node instead of being orphaned; the entry is relabelled `name@range` (#4569, #4572, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah; reported by @BiSide).
- Feature: **yaml** `.yaml`/`.yml` files are now extracted structurally (a file node plus `contains` edges to keys) and classified as code rather than documents, so Helm charts, Kubernetes manifests, and CI pipelines contribute nodes to a code-only or `--update` run instead of nothing, matching how `.json` is handled. Multi-document streams (`---` separators) are walked per document; a data array, an OpenAPI/Swagger spec, a JSON-schema-in-YAML, and a flat data bundle are skipped so data-heavy YAML does not mint orphan nodes; parsing uses `safe_load` so a `!!python/...` tag never executes; output is bounded (1 MiB, 500 pairs, depth 6). The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts (#2214, #4706, thanks @nothariharan; reported by @dchavezf).
- Fix: **extract** a bare call that resolves to a same-named symbol only because the caller imported that symbol's module (`from b import other`, then a call to a `_make_id` defined in both `a.py` and `b.py`) is no longer promoted to `EXTRACTED`; the edge is still emitted for connectivity but stays `INFERRED`, so a symbol that was never imported is not falsely certified. A real symbol import (`from a import _make_id`) still resolves `EXTRACTED` (#2945, #4707, thanks @nothariharan; reported by @TotalUnitManagement).
- Fix: **security** the SSRF guard blocks a host that resolves to a multicast address (`224.0.0.0/4`, `ff00::/8`), closing a gap alongside the existing private/reserved/loopback/link-local checks (#4708, thanks @Dextheking1).
- Fix: **security** the Obsidian export sanitizes a node's file-type and confidence before emitting them as frontmatter `tags`, so a crafted value cannot break out of the YAML list into a sibling key, matching how community tags are already sanitized (#4709, thanks @Dextheking1).
- Fix: **security** the Google Workspace shortcut sidecar escapes a file id or url through full YAML double-quoted-scalar escaping (tab, C0/DEL controls, and the Unicode line breaks U+2028/U+2029/U+0085), so a hostile shortcut file cannot inject frontmatter keys (#4710, thanks @Dextheking1).
- Fix: **affected** `graphify affected <path>` resolves a path whose file-node label was disambiguated by the shared-basename suffix pass (for example two `hooks.py` from different directories), reusing the canonical file-label predicate instead of a bare basename match (#4698, #4713, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah; reported by @karsan8119).
- Fix: **build** a raw (`--no-cluster`) build resolves an import endpoint through the same old-stem alias index the clustered build uses, and mints an external stub only after resolution, so the raw graph no longer freezes an import onto a stub when the clustered graph resolves it (#4670, #4676, thanks @nothariharan; reported by @xiongjianxu).
- Fix: **cross-repo** an Objective-C class declared in one repo's header and implemented in another repo's `.m` binds a member call to the implementation, the cross-repo analog of the same-repo split-dir fix; two same-named classes that both define the selector stay ambiguous (#4690, #4691, thanks @xiongjianxu).
- Fix: **hooks** the rebuild hook runs from the checkout's top level (derived from the git common dir, falling back to `--show-toplevel`), so a stray `graphify-out/` in a subdirectory can no longer root the rebuild at the wrong place and walk an enormous tree (#3258, #4689, thanks @jaimemartinez; reported by @dsfaccini).
- Fix: **objc** `NS_CLOSED_ENUM` declarations are extracted as enums with their cases, the same as `NS_ENUM`/`NS_OPTIONS`; the AST cache schema is bumped so the first build after upgrading re-extracts (#4705, thanks @Jvxoq).
- Fix: **sql** a `CREATE TABLE` whose column default the SQL grammar cannot parse (for example MySQL/MariaDB `DEFAULT current_timestamp()`) is recovered from the ERROR node instead of being dropped, so the table and its foreign-key references still resolve; the AST cache schema is bumped (#4613, #4677, thanks @08raviyadav; reported by @AirRunner).
